purpose: How a licensed life insurance agent turns placed cases into a durable, compounding book: measuring persistency by issue cohort rather than by a book-wide average, understanding renewal, trail and chargeback compensation as carrier-specific mechanisms whose terms are read from the contract rather than assumed, running the post-delivery onboarding, billing hygiene, early-warning and grace-period interventions that keep policies in force, holding beneficiary and ownership records current so the benefit reaches the people the policy was bought for, serving death claims as the moment the whole book exists for, operating a segmented service cadence sized against real capacity, running documented annual reviews that read in-force ledgers honestly and watch contractual option windows that expire silently, gating the passage from servicing into selling so a review is never a pretext for a sale, and earning referrals and orphan-block servicing rights on evidenced service so the book grows by compounding instead of churning.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the operator is an individual producer or very small agency servicing a personal book of in-force life business, already licensed and appointed, with the case already delivered; licensing, affiliation and the sale itself are the sibling knowledge bases' territory and are treated here as preconditions

renewal duration, trail basis, vesting, advance and chargeback recovery rules differ by carrier, product, contract level, issue year and jurisdiction, so every one of them is described here as a mechanism to be read off the operator's own compensation schedule and contract before it is relied on, never as a figure this knowledge base supplies

policy provisions named here (grace, reinstatement, non-forfeiture, conversion privilege, level-period expiry, contestability, settlement options) are contract classes whose exact terms, timeframes and requirements are set by the individual contract and its jurisdiction and must be read on the actual policy for the actual client

record retention, privacy, replacement, advertising, do-not-contact, inducement and referral-compensation obligations are named here as obligation classes only; their current specifics differ by state and by carrier and must be verified with the relevant insurance department, the carrier's compliance manual and counsel before acting

in-force values shown on a current-assumption basis are projections under stated assumptions and are never treated, presented or implied as promises; only the guaranteed basis is contractually promised
everything here is educational and operational knowledge for the agent's own practice; it is not personalized financial, insurance, tax, legal or medical advice for any specific consumer
exclusions: the producer licensing path and its continuing obligations, resident and nonresident footprint, carrier contracting and appointment, captive versus independent versus marketing-organization affiliation, who contractually owns or vests the book, contract level and upline economics, carrier and product-shelf selection, market-focus choice and prospect lead generation to strangers - that is the licensing, carrier selection and market focus knowledge base, whose contract terms this one takes as given inputs

fact-finding and needs analysis, term versus permanent product mechanics, sizing a death benefit, matching product to need under suitability and best-interest standards, the recommendation file, illustration presentation at the point of sale, the replacement transaction and its disclosure process, application completion, underwriting, offer variance and the policy delivery meeting including the right to examine - that is the needs analysis, product fit and suitability knowledge base this one receives finished cases from and routes new recommendations back into

personalized financial, investment, tax, legal, estate or medical advice to any client or beneficiary, including how to invest or use claim proceeds and any drafting or interpretation of trusts, wills, buy-sell agreements or divorce decrees

any promise, projection presented as a promise, or performance guarantee on cash-value, indexed or variable products; current-assumption ledger columns are projections and are never presented as expected outcomes

specific commission, renewal, trail, override or chargeback percentages, advance terms, persistency benchmark rates, lead prices, book valuation multiples, case sizes or income figures; every one of these appears only as a mechanism to be computed or verified from the operator's own contracts, carrier statements and measured results
claims adjudication itself, contest or rescission decisions, and any advocacy that amounts to practising law on a beneficiary's behalf; the agent assists with filing and expectation-setting only
recruiting other producers, building a downline, and the economics of overrides earned on other agents' production or on their in-force blocks
securities, advisory or registered-product activity, including recommendations on variable contracts that require separate registration, and any management of client investments

jurisdiction-specific record-retention periods, privacy statute requirements, do-not-contact and inducement or rebating specifics, and carrier reinstatement or agent-of-record forms and timeframes, which appear here only as obligation classes to verify against current rules in each jurisdiction and each carrier's manual
buying, selling or valuing a book of business in currency terms, and negotiating the purchase price or terms of a block transfer

competency_questions.question: Why is persistency rather than submitted production the thing that decides what this practice is worth in five years, and how do I measure it on my own book so the number is reproducible?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOOK_ASSET_FRAME states what the in-force book is and the horizon decisions are judged on; PERSISTENCY_MEASUREMENT defines the departure-event taxonomy, issue-cohort grouping and count-versus-premium weighting and requires the carrier's own published window to be adopted and recorded; PERSISTENCY_DIAGNOSTIC_LOOP shows how a measured decline is turned into a located cause

competency_questions.question: How does money actually keep arriving on a policy after the first year, what conditions it, and what makes it stop?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RENEWAL_AND_TRAIL_MECHANICS names renewal, service and trail compensation as per-carrier per-product mechanisms with duration, computation basis, conditioning and vesting read from the actual schedule and contract, names the policy events that alter or end the stream, and supplies no percentage of its own

competency_questions.question: What is my chargeback exposure right now, what does one lapsed policy actually cost me all in, and how do I run the practice so a normal cluster of early terminations is absorbable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHARGEBACK_EXPOSURE_LEDGER describes advance-versus-earned mechanics, unearned exposure by issue vintage, the carrier's stated recovery rule and reconciliation against the carrier statement; LAPSE_COST_ACCOUNTING enumerates the cost components and requires each to be sourced from the practice's own records

competency_questions.question: Which policies in my book are most likely to terminate in the next few months, and how would I know before a lapse notice arrives?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EARLY_DURATION_RISK_MAP names the structural drivers of early termination and requires cases to be scored at issue; LAPSE_WARNING_SYSTEM lists the carrier-side and client-side signals, maps each to an action and an owner, and requires a compensating check where a carrier does not notify

competency_questions.question: What has to happen in the weeks right after the policy is delivered so that it survives its first year?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POST_DELIVERY_ONBOARDING specifies the confirmation sequence ending in a written client confirmation and a file note; BILLING_AND_PAYMENT_HYGIENE explains mode, method and draft-date selection as persistency levers including the modal-loading mechanism read off the rate page

competency_questions.question: A client's payment failed and the policy is in the grace period - what are the options, in what order, and when is reinstating better for the client than being rewritten?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GRACE_AND_REINSTATEMENT_PLAY names grace, automatic premium loan and non-forfeiture provisions and the reinstatement process as contract classes to read on the actual policy, requires the cause of non-payment to be found before a fix is proposed, and states why a rewrite that restarts underwriting and contestability is usually worse for the client than reinstatement

competency_questions.question: How do I handle routine in-force service requests without stalling the client, and where does an administrative change become a recommendation I must analyse first?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVICE_REQUEST_DESK lists the request types with form, signature, proof and confirmation requirements and states the boundary test that sends coverage-, cost- or benefit-changing requests through the suitability process; BENEFICIARY_RECORD_HYGIENE states the verification cycle and the carrier-record-governs mechanism; BOOK_RECORDS_AND_CONTINUITY states what must be logged and retained

competency_questions.question: A client has died - what exactly do I do for the family, in what order, and what am I not permitted to do?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLAIM_SUPPORT_PROTOCOL gives the response sequence, the document classes the carrier will require, honest expectation-setting including what a contestable-period review means, settlement options explained as classes without steering, and the explicit prohibitions on tax, legal and investment advice and on selling at the claim

competency_questions.question: How many client relationships can I actually serve at the cadence I have promised, and what makes this book servable by anyone other than me?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVICE_CADENCE_AND_CAPACITY gives the need-based segmentation, the cadence classes and the contact-volume-to-hours arithmetic with slack for claims, and names the honest responses when the promise does not fit; BOOK_RECORDS_AND_CONTINUITY names the record content, retention and privacy obligation classes and the successor arrangement

competency_questions.question: What belongs in an annual policy review, and how do I read an in-force ledger honestly when the current-assumption columns look better than the guarantees?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ANNUAL_POLICY_REVIEW fixes the agenda and the documented file-note output and states that a review with nothing sold is a successful review; INFORCE_LEDGER_INTERPRETATION separates guaranteed from current-assumption columns, names the erosion mechanisms, and forbids presenting a projection as an expectation or mixing bases across a comparison

competency_questions.question: Which contractual deadlines and life events must I be watching on behalf of clients who are not watching them themselves?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONVERSION_AND_DEADLINE_WATCH enumerates the dated option classes, requires each to be read from the actual contract and entered as an alert far enough ahead to allow underwriting time, and states the irreversibility of a missed window; LIFE_EVENT_TRIGGER_MAP catalogues the events and the deliberate listening system that catches them without manufacturing urgency

competency_questions.question: When a review turns up something I could sell, how do I keep the review a service rather than a pretext, and what must be disclosed before anything changes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REVIEW_TO_SALE_ETHICS_GATE states the documented-change precondition, the write-it-first rule, the do-nothing baseline, compensation disclosure on both sides of the decision, the handoff of any replacement to the suitability knowledge base's process, and the prohibited pressure techniques including fear framing and pressing a client showing confusion or duress

competency_questions.question: How do I build a referral flow that compounds without pressuring clients or paying for introductions in ways that are not permitted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REFERRAL_SYSTEM_DESIGN ties the ask to an evidenced service outcome, makes refusal costless, forbids conditioning service on referrals, and names inducement, rebating and referral-compensation limits as classes to verify; CENTER_OF_INFLUENCE_NETWORK adds the professional-partner mechanics and the compensation-sharing and privacy boundaries

competency_questions.question: Should I take on an orphan block or accept an agent-of-record change, and what actually transfers when I do?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ORPHAN_AND_AGENT_OF_RECORD describes the policyowner-authorized carrier-administered change process, separates servicing responsibility from the compensation stream and requires both to be verified per carrier and contract, tests the block against measured capacity and record condition, and states the conduct prohibitions on disparagement, unrequested changes and bundling a servicing change with a replacement

glossary.definition: The share of issued policies (or of the premium they represent) still in force at a stated point after issue. It is only meaningful with its definition attached: the measurement window, whether it counts policies or premium, and which departure events are excluded. Carriers and distributors each publish it on windows they define themselves, so the operator adopts the definition their carrier actually uses and records it beside the number.

Termination of a policy for non-payment of premium after the grace period ends, as distinct from a surrender (the owner voluntarily ends the contract, taking any cash value), a non-taken case (issued but never paid for), a non-forfeiture election (coverage continues in reduced form without further premium), an expiry (a term contract reaching the end of its coverage or level period) and a death claim. Merging these into one number makes a persistency report unusable.

The carrier's recovery of compensation already paid but not yet earned when a policy terminates early. The recovery may be full or pro-rata depending on how soon the termination occurs and what the agent's contract says, and it is taken from later commissions or billed directly, creating a debit balance until it is cleared. The rule is contract-specific and must be read per carrier.

Compensation paid on premiums received in policy durations after the first, typically for a stated number of durations and often conditioned on the agent remaining appointed or on vesting terms. Its duration, computation basis and conditions vary by carrier, product and contract and are read off the compensation schedule, never assumed.

Continuing compensation computed on an ongoing basis for as long as the policy or account persists - on premium received, on account or fund value, or on another contract measure depending on product type. It rewards keeping business in force rather than placing it, which is why it is the compensation form most aligned with the book as a durable asset.

The contractual window after a missed premium during which the policy remains in force and the overdue premium can still be paid. Its length and its interaction with any automatic premium loan or non-forfeiture provision are set by the individual contract and must be read on the actual policy.

The carrier-defined process for restoring a lapsed policy, generally requiring an application, payment of back premium with any interest, and evidence of insurability, available only within a period stated in the contract. It preserves the original contract, its issue-age pricing and its elapsed contestability, which is usually why it serves a client better than being rewritten.

Provisions in a policy with cash value that let coverage continue without further premium - typically a reduced paid-up amount or extended term coverage - or be surrendered for its cash value. Electing one is a coverage change, not an administrative change, so it belongs on the recommendation side of the service boundary.

A current re-projection of a permanent policy requested from the carrier, showing values on both a guaranteed basis and a current-assumption basis given the policy's actual funding and status to date. It answers what happens if nothing changes; only the guaranteed columns are contractually promised.

The producer the carrier recognizes as servicing a given policy. Changing it is a carrier-administered process that generally requires the policyowner's own written authorization on the carrier's form, and it moves servicing responsibility without necessarily moving any compensation stream - what transfers is set by the carrier's rules and the agency contract and must be verified case by case.

nodes.definition: Fix, before any retention tactic is chosen, what the book actually is for this practice and over what horizon its decisions are judged. The book is the set of policies currently in force, the households behind them, the servicing role the carrier recognizes the agent in on each, and the compensation that continues to arrive while those policies keep paying. The frame states the economic asymmetry that everything downstream rests on: first-year compensation is payment for work already done and is consumed as it arrives, while the renewal and trail stream, the referral flow from served clients, and the standing permission to serve the same household again are the only components that compound. Any decision that raises this month's submitted production while lowering the probability that a policy is still paying several years from now therefore shrinks the asset, however good the month looks. The frame also separates what the operator controls from what the contract hands them: vesting, ownership and release terms are settled in the affiliation agreement and are taken here as given inputs, while whether policies persist and whether clients would take the agent's call are entirely within this practice's control.

included: what counts as the in-force book and the horizon decisions are judged against
the distinction between consumed first-year cash and compounding renewal, referral and service value
separating operator-controlled persistency from contract-given ownership terms
excluded: negotiating vesting, release or contract level with an upline or carrier
carrier, product-shelf or market-focus selection
valuing the book in currency terms or negotiating a block sale

pros.claim: Naming the judging horizon converts retention from an optional courtesy into the practice's primary economic activity
pros.example: an agent who judges a month by cases still paying at their first anniversary rather than by applications submitted stops writing premium the household was never going to sustain

pros.claim: Separating controllables from contract-given terms stops the operator from either assuming a stream they do not own or neglecting one they do
pros.example: reading the affiliation agreement once and recording that renewals continue only under stated conditions, then building the service program on what actually persists

cons.claim: A long-horizon frame can excuse unmeasured service work, letting an unprofitable book feel virtuous
cons.example: spending most of a week on courtesy calls into a segment that produces neither improved persistency nor a single introduction

failure_modes: treating the book as a list of past sales rather than a live set of obligations owed to households
assuming the renewal stream is owned when the affiliation agreement conditions or forfeits it
judging the practice on applications submitted, which rewards exactly the cases most likely to lapse
acceptance_tests: the written frame names what counts as in force, the horizon decisions are judged on, and which terms are contract-given rather than chosen
every retention initiative running in the practice can be traced back to the horizon this frame sets rather than to a monthly production target
revisit_triggers: the affiliation agreement, its vesting terms or the compensation basis changes
the practice adds a product class whose compensation behaves differently over the policy's life
the book's size or composition changes enough that the horizon assumptions no longer hold

base.update_signal: the affiliation agreement, the product mix, or the horizon the practice judges itself on changes

nodes.definition: Build the measurement before the retention program, because a number nobody can reproduce cannot be managed. First separate the departure events that look alike on a report and are not the same failure: a non-taken case that never paid a premium, a lapse for non-payment after grace, an owner-requested surrender, an election of a non-forfeiture option that keeps reduced coverage alive, a term contract reaching the end of its coverage or level period, a conversion into a permanent contract, and a death claim - the last of which is the book doing its job and must never be counted as a loss. Then group policies by the month they were placed and track each cohort forward, because a single book-wide ratio hides the case where last quarter's business is failing while older business holds. Keep both a policy-count view and a premium-weighted view, since a few large cases can move the money while the count looks stable. Finally, adopt the persistency window your carrier or distributor actually publishes rather than inventing one, and store the definition beside the number - the window, the weighting, the exclusions - so that a later comparison against a carrier report or against your own earlier result means anything.

included: the departure-event taxonomy
issue-cohort grouping and forward tracking
count versus premium weighting
adopting and recording the carrier's published window and exclusions
excluded: diagnosing why a cohort failed
setting service cadence or retention tactics
computing the money at risk behind a lapse

pros.claim: Cohort measurement localizes a problem to the business that caused it instead of averaging it into invisibility
pros.example: a weak first-duration cohort that traces to one lead source and one month, while every older cohort holds steady

pros.claim: Storing the definition beside the number makes carrier reports and internal reports comparable instead of arguable
pros.example: recognizing that a carrier's figure excludes non-taken cases while the internal figure includes them, so the gap is definitional rather than real

cons.claim: A small book produces noisy cohort rates that invite over-reaction to ordinary variation
cons.example: two lapses in a light issue month reading as a collapse and triggering an expensive program change that the next cohort shows was unnecessary

failure_modes: mixing non-taken cases and death claims into the lapse count so the number cannot be acted on
comparing an internal ratio to a carrier ratio computed on a different window and drawing a false conclusion
reporting only a book-wide average, which always lags the problem by the age of the book
acceptance_tests: every departure in the last period is classified into exactly one named outcome, with death claims recorded separately from losses
the stored measurement definition names the window, the weighting and the exclusions, and matches the definition used by the carrier report it is compared against
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes its published persistency definition or reporting window
the product mix shifts enough that older cohorts are no longer comparable to new ones
the book grows past the point where cohort samples stop being noise-dominated

base.update_signal: a carrier restates its persistency definition, or the book's product mix or volume changes enough to invalidate cohort comparisons

nodes.definition: Understand, per carrier and per product actually on the shelf, the mechanism by which money continues to arrive after the first year and the conditions under which it stops. The mechanism classes are stable even though every number attached to them is not: first-year compensation paid on the initial premium; renewal compensation paid on premiums received in later durations, usually for a stated number of durations; service or trail compensation computed on a continuing basis - on premium received, on account or fund value, or on another contract measure depending on product type; and the vesting terms that decide whether any of it survives termination of the appointment or a move to another distributor. For each product on the shelf, read from the current compensation schedule and the contract itself how long renewals run, on what basis they are computed, whether they are conditioned on continued appointment or on production requirements, whether payment arrives advanced or as earned, and what a mid-life policy change does to the stream - a face reduction, a mode change, a non-forfeiture election, a conversion, a loan or a partial withdrawal can each alter or end it. No percentage is portable between carriers, products, contract levels or issue years; the durable knowledge is the shape of each mechanism plus the habit of verifying the specific terms before any forecast leans on them.

included: renewal, service and trail compensation as per-carrier mechanisms
the conditioning and vesting questions to answer per product
policy events that alter or end a continuing stream
the verify-before-forecasting habit
excluded: choosing carriers by their compensation schedule or negotiating contract level
first-year selling compensation as a shelf-selection criterion
any specific percentage, rate or income figure

pros.claim: Knowing which products keep paying after placement shows which parts of the book actually build the asset and which only look productive
pros.example: recognizing that a product whose renewals run only a short duration cannot fund the multi-year service cadence its buyers will need

pros.claim: Reading the schedule per product kills the most common forecasting error in a young practice
pros.example: an agent who assumed a peer's renewal terms applied to their own contract discovering the difference before budgeting on it rather than after

cons.claim: Compensation-continuation knowledge creates a standing temptation to let the agent's income shape what sits on the shelf or what gets recommended
cons.example: favouring the contract with the longer renewal tail when the household's actual objective points at a different product class

failure_modes: quoting a renewal expectation from memory, from a recruiter's pitch, or from another agent's contract
assuming renewals survive termination without having read the vesting language
overlooking that an ordinary service transaction can reset or extinguish the continuing stream
acceptance_tests: for every product on the shelf there is a recorded, sourced answer to how long renewals run, on what basis they are computed, what conditions them, and what a policy change does to them
no figure in any practice forecast is used unless it was read from a current compensation schedule and dated
revisit_triggers: a carrier reissues or amends its compensation schedule
a product is added to or withdrawn from the shelf
the practice's contract level or distribution relationship changes

base.update_signal: a carrier amends its compensation schedule or vesting terms, or the practice's contract or product shelf changes

nodes.definition: Keep a running ledger of money the practice has been paid but has not yet earned, and of the recovery that would follow an early termination. The mechanism: when compensation is advanced, the carrier pays against premium it expects to receive over a future period and earns the advance down as premium actually arrives; if the policy terminates before the advance is earned, the unearned portion becomes a debit balance the carrier recovers out of later commissions or bills directly, and whether the recovery is full or pro-rata depends on how soon the termination occurs and on what the agent's contract says. The work unit is to know at any moment the unearned advance by issue vintage, each carrier's stated recovery rule, and the concentration risk carried by any single large case - and to reconcile all of it against the carrier's own commission statement every cycle rather than trusting an internal estimate, because the carrier's ledger is the one that will be enforced. The practice's cash is then run so that an ordinary cluster of early terminations is an absorbable planned cost rather than a solvency event, which is what makes it possible to give a client the honest answer when their policy is in trouble.

included: advance-versus-earned mechanics
unearned exposure tracked by issue vintage
per-carrier recovery rules and statement reconciliation
concentration risk and cash planning against exposure
excluded: negotiating advance terms or contract level with a distributor
the full economic cost of a lapse beyond the carrier recovery
any specific advance percentage or recovery rate

pros.claim: A reconciled exposure ledger turns chargebacks from a shock into a planned, reservable cost
pros.example: seeing that one issue vintage carries most of the unearned advance and holding cash against it before the notices arrive

pros.claim: Knowing the exposure in advance protects the client, because an agent who cannot afford the truth gives worse advice
pros.example: an agent with a reserve can recommend the reinstatement that generates them nothing, where an agent facing a debit balance feels the pull toward a rewrite

cons.claim: Exposure aversion can push a practice into as-earned payment that starves it of the working capital its service program needs
cons.example: refusing advances entirely and then having no funds to staff the review cadence the book was sold on

cons.claim: A ledger maintained internally without reconciliation drifts from the carrier's own accounting and gives false comfort
cons.example: an internal estimate that omits a carrier's fee handling and understates the balance actually owed

failure_modes: treating advanced compensation as earned income and spending it
learning a carrier's recovery rule only after the first debit balance appears
netting exposure across carriers that settle independently, hiding a concentration in one of them
acceptance_tests: the ledger shows unearned advance by issue vintage and per carrier, and reconciles to the latest carrier commission statement within the practice's stated tolerance
each carrier's recovery rule and its stated window are recorded from the contract with a date, not from recollection
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes its advance, earning or recovery terms
a debit balance appears that the ledger did not anticipate
issue volume or average case size shifts enough to change concentration risk

base.update_signal: a carrier amends its advance or chargeback recovery terms, or a reconciliation gap appears against a commission statement

nodes.definition: Price a lost policy properly, using only figures the practice can source from its own records, so that retention spending is decided by arithmetic instead of by anxiety. The components are structural and each is computable in-house: the unearned advance the carrier will recover; the renewal and trail compensation that will now never arrive over the remaining durations for that product; the acquisition cost already spent on that household, taken from the practice's own lead ledger and time records; the cost of writing a replacement case to stand in its place, which is the same acquisition cost paid again plus the underwriting cycle; and the loss that never shows on a statement - a household that will not refer, may not answer again, and whose beneficiaries are now uninsured against the risk they were protected from. The output is a per-lapse cost band the practice actually believes, which then decides how much retention effort is rational and where it belongs: a save whose cost sits below the loss it prevents is obviously worth doing, and the same arithmetic exposes the retention gestures that are theatre. No industry benchmark is imported for any component; if a component cannot be sourced from the practice's records it is carried as an explicit unknown rather than as a guessed number.

included: the cost components of a lost policy
sourcing every component from the practice's own ledger, calendar and carrier statements
using the resulting band to size retention effort
excluded: imported industry benchmarks, published lapse costs or assumed acquisition figures
book valuation for sale
the diagnosis of why the cohort lapsed

pros.claim: A believable per-lapse cost converts retention from a virtue into a budgeted activity with a decision rule
pros.example: an agent who knows what a lost case costs can justify the hours spent chasing a failed draft, and can equally justify stopping a mailing that saves nothing

cons.claim: The largest components are the least measurable, so the band can be built mostly of soft estimates and then treated as precise
cons.example: assigning a confident figure to lost referral flow that no record in the practice supports

cons.claim: Cost-per-lapse thinking can drift into pressuring clients whose policies genuinely no longer serve them
cons.example: working hard to keep a household paying for coverage whose original purpose ended, because the loss is expensive to the agent

failure_modes: importing an industry lapse-cost figure and presenting it as this practice's number
counting only the chargeback and ignoring the forfeited renewal stream and reacquisition cost
using the number to justify retention pressure rather than retention service
acceptance_tests: every component of the cost band traces to a record inside the practice, and components that cannot be sourced are shown as explicit unknowns rather than estimates
at least one retention activity has been started or stopped on the strength of the resulting comparison
revisit_triggers: acquisition cost or case mix changes materially
a carrier's renewal duration or recovery rule changes, altering the forfeited stream
the practice's measured save rate changes enough to alter the effort comparison

base.update_signal: the practice's measured acquisition cost, save rate, case mix or a carrier's renewal terms change

nodes.definition: Map the concentrated failure zone that follows issue and name its drivers individually, so they can be attacked one at a time rather than as a vague persistency problem. The recurring drivers are structural rather than mysterious: a premium set at the outer edge of what the household can sustain, so any shock ends it; a payment mechanism that was never actually exercised, where the first draft fails, a card has expired or a bank account has changed; a client who did not understand what they bought, what it costs or what the first statement would look like; a case sold against an urgency the client never really owned; a household whose income, employment or living situation changed between application and delivery; a competing agent's replacement approach arriving into a relationship with no service history to defend it; and product features the client discovers later and dislikes. The work is to score every issued case against these drivers at delivery - not after a notice arrives - so the watchlist is populated in advance and the highest-risk cases receive the onboarding attention they need while intervention is still cheap and the relationship is still warm.

included: the driver taxonomy for early termination
scoring issued cases against the drivers at delivery
prioritizing onboarding attention by risk
excluded: the point-of-sale suitability and affordability analysis itself
the operational save playbook once a policy is already in grace
carrier-side notice mechanics

pros.claim: Naming drivers separately turns an unmanageable ratio into a short list of fixable failures
pros.example: discovering that failed first drafts and unexercised payment mechanisms account for most early losses, which is an operations fix rather than a sales problem

pros.claim: Scoring at delivery buys intervention time while it is still cheap and welcome
pros.example: flagging a household whose income changed during underwriting and confirming the premium is still comfortable before the second payment rather than after the lapse notice

cons.claim: Risk scoring can harden into profiling that quietly under-serves clients who were never actually at risk
cons.example: treating every modest-premium household as fragile and giving the segment less attention than the drivers justify

failure_modes: treating early termination as a single undifferentiated problem and responding with generic contact
scoring risk only after the first missed payment, when the cheapest interventions have already expired
recording a driver without assigning anyone the action that addresses it
acceptance_tests: every case issued in the last period carries a risk note naming which drivers apply to it and which do not
each named driver maps to a specific onboarding or watchlist action with an owner
revisit_triggers: a cohort fails for a reason not present in the driver list
a new product, lead source or market segment enters the book
the diagnostic loop reassigns a loss cause to a stage the map does not cover

base.update_signal: a cohort fails for a driver absent from the map, or a new product, segment or lead source enters the book

nodes.definition: Run a defined sequence in the weeks immediately after the contract is delivered whose only purpose is to convert a signed case into a policy that survives its first year. The sequence confirms that the payment mechanism is live, correctly dated against the household's actual cash flow, and has successfully collected at least once; sets the expectation of exactly what the first carrier communication will look like, when it will arrive and what it will say, so the client is not startled into cancelling by a routine notice; restates in plain language what the policy does and does not do, using the same words that were used at the sale rather than new ones; verifies owner and beneficiary as actually recorded on the issued contract rather than as intended on the application; captures every contact channel plus the client's own stated preference for how and when to be contacted; records a secondary or trusted contact where the client is willing and where the carrier and jurisdiction permit; and books the first review with a date rather than an intention. It closes with a short written confirmation to the client and a dated file note. The delivery meeting itself, the contract comparison and the right-to-examine explanation belong to the case knowledge base; this unit begins the moment the delivered policy becomes a standing obligation.

included: confirming the payment mechanism has actually collected
setting first-statement expectations
verifying issued owner and beneficiary records
capturing channels, preferences and a trusted contact where permitted
booking the first review and writing the file note
excluded: the delivery meeting, contract comparison and right-to-examine explanation
any new recommendation or additional sale during onboarding
the underwriting or issue process

pros.claim: Confirming a successful first collection removes the single most preventable cause of early termination
pros.example: catching a transposed account number on a bank draft in the first cycle, while the client is still expecting the policy to start

pros.claim: Setting the expectation of the first carrier notice stops routine paperwork from reading as a problem
pros.example: a client who was told a premium notice would arrive filing it instead of calling to cancel a policy they thought had gone wrong

cons.claim: A heavy onboarding sequence consumes exactly the hours a growing practice wants to spend on new business, and the pressure to skip it is strongest when it matters most
cons.example: a busy month where onboarding calls are deferred on the cases written under the most affordability strain

cons.claim: Contact so soon after the sale can be read as pressure for another sale unless its service purpose is explicit
cons.example: a client who assumes the follow-up call is an upsell and stops answering the phone

failure_modes: assuming the payment mechanism works because the application said it would
onboarding from the application data rather than from the issued contract, so a change made in underwriting is never noticed
leaving the first review as an intention with no date, which means it never happens
acceptance_tests: for every case delivered in the period the file records a confirmed first collection, the client's confirmed contact preferences, and owner and beneficiary verified against the issued contract
each onboarded case has a dated first review in the calendar and a written confirmation sent to the client
revisit_triggers: early-duration losses appear among cases that completed onboarding
a carrier changes its billing communications or first-notice timing
a new product is added whose first-year client experience differs materially

base.update_signal: early losses appear among onboarded cases, or a carrier changes its first-year billing communications

nodes.definition: Treat the way premium is collected as a persistency instrument rather than an administrative detail, because the commonest way a policy dies is that a payment stopped arriving, not that a client decided to be uninsured. The levers are mode (how often premium is billed), method (bank draft, card, direct bill, list or payroll deduction), the draft date relative to the household's pay cycle and other fixed obligations, and who gets notified when a collection fails. The mechanisms are worth knowing precisely: carriers apply a modal loading so that paying more frequently generally raises the total annual outlay for identical coverage, with the size of the loading set per carrier and product and readable on the rate page rather than assumed; direct-billed policies depend on a person remembering, which is the weakest link available; cards expire and are reissued on their own schedule while bank accounts change on another; list and payroll billing survives only as long as the employment does; and a returned collection starts a clock the client frequently does not notice. The work is to choose mode, method and date deliberately at issue, to re-verify the mechanism whenever banking, employment, address or marital status changes, and to treat a single failed collection as an event requiring contact rather than as a routine that will resolve itself.

included: mode, method and draft-date selection as retention levers
the modal-loading mechanism read from the rate page
re-verification triggers when banking or employment changes
treating a failed collection as a contact event
excluded: setting the premium level or affordability analysis at the point of sale
carrier accounting or reconciliation of remitted premium
any specific modal factor or fee figure

pros.claim: Aligning the draft date and method to the household's cash cycle removes failures that have nothing to do with willingness to pay
pros.example: moving a draft off the end of the month, where a household's fixed obligations cluster, to just after payday

pros.claim: Knowing the modal-loading mechanism lets the agent explain honestly why a monthly habit costs more over a year
pros.example: showing a client the rate page rather than asserting a saving, then letting them choose the mode they will actually sustain

cons.claim: Optimizing for the lowest total outlay can push a household onto an annual mode it cannot budget for, producing a larger single failure
cons.example: an annual premium falling due in a month the household has other large obligations, ending a policy that monthly billing would have carried

cons.claim: Automatic collection hides disengagement, so a policy can keep paying while the relationship quietly dies
cons.example: a client who has moved, changed their name and never been re-contacted because nothing ever failed

failure_modes: choosing mode by what makes the premium look smallest at the sale rather than by what the household will sustain
leaving a policy on direct bill by default for a client who has never in their life remembered a bill
treating a returned collection as a carrier matter rather than as the first signal of a lapse
acceptance_tests: every in-force policy records its mode, method, draft date and the date the mechanism was last verified
a failed collection generates a contact attempt within the practice's stated response window, logged whether or not it reached the client
revisit_triggers: a client reports a change of bank, employer, address or marital status
a carrier changes its billing methods, retry behaviour or notice timing
failed collections cluster on a particular method, mode or draft date

base.update_signal: failed collections cluster on one method, mode or date, or a carrier changes its billing and retry behaviour

nodes.definition: Assemble every signal that a policy is drifting toward termination into one dated watchlist, each entry carrying a trigger, an owner, a response window and a logged outcome. The carrier-side signals include returned or declined collections, late-payment and grace notices, lapse-pending notices, requests for a mode or method change, requests to reduce face amount, loan and partial-withdrawal requests on permanent contracts, non-forfeiture election notices, and mail returned as undeliverable. The client-side signals are softer and arrive through the relationship: unanswered contacts across every channel, a mentioned job loss, a separation, a move, a hospitalization, a new large obligation, or the sentence about the premium getting hard that a client drops at the end of a call. Part of the work is structural rather than reactive: carriers deliver notices through their own portals, downloads and mailings on their own schedules and with their own gaps, so the practice must know which of its carriers actually notify it, how quickly, and build a compensating periodic check for the ones that do not. Every trigger maps to a defined first action, every attempt is logged whether or not it reached anyone, and no client is worked harder than their recorded contact preferences allow.

included: the carrier-side and client-side signal inventory
per-carrier notification reality and compensating checks
trigger to action to owner mapping with logged attempts
respecting recorded contact preferences while working the list
excluded: the intervention conversation and the reinstatement decision itself
diagnosing systemic cohort causes
prospecting contact to non-clients

pros.claim: A single dated watchlist converts scattered carrier notices into work that actually gets done by a named person
pros.example: a returned-draft notice arriving in a portal on a Friday still producing a contact attempt inside the response window rather than being seen after the grace period has run

pros.claim: Knowing which carriers notify slowly or not at all lets the practice cover the gap instead of discovering it through a lost policy
pros.example: adding a monthly in-force status pull for a carrier whose notices arrive only by mail to the client and never to the agent

cons.claim: Signal-driven outreach can become intrusive and read as harassment, especially against a client who is embarrassed about money
cons.example: repeated calls and messages after a failed draft to a household in temporary hardship that had asked to be contacted only by email

cons.claim: The list generates volume that competes with scheduled reviews and claim work for the same hours
cons.example: a heavy notice week displacing the reviews booked at onboarding, which then slip a quarter

failure_modes: relying on carrier notices reaching the agent when several carriers notify only the policyowner
logging triggers without owners or response windows, so the list becomes a record of things nobody did
working the list past the client's stated contact preferences and damaging the relationship the policy depends on
acceptance_tests: every carrier on the shelf has a recorded answer to what it notifies, to whom, through which channel and how quickly, plus a compensating check where the answer is inadequate
each watchlist entry in the last period shows a trigger, an owner, an attempted action inside the response window, and a logged outcome
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes its notice channels, content or timing
a lapse occurs that produced no watchlist entry
the practice's response-window performance degrades as the book grows

base.update_signal: a carrier changes its notification behaviour, or a lapse occurs that the watchlist never flagged

nodes.definition: Work the narrow window between a missed payment and a permanently lost contract with a decision procedure settled in advance, because it will always be executed under time pressure. The contract mechanisms to read on the actual policy: the grace period during which coverage continues and the overdue premium can still be paid; on contracts with cash value, an automatic premium loan or non-forfeiture provision that may keep some coverage alive without payment; and reinstatement, a carrier-defined process that generally requires an application, payment of back premium with any interest, and evidence of insurability, available only within a period the contract states - every one of these terms varies by contract, product and jurisdiction and must be verified rather than recited. The client-side procedure is fixed: find out why the payment stopped before proposing any fix, because a temporary cash gap, a bank change and a decision that the coverage is no longer wanted call for three different answers; present the honest option set - cure the overdue premium, change mode or method to something sustainable, reduce coverage to what the household can carry, elect a non-forfeiture option, reinstate, or let it go with a clear statement of what is lost; and explain plainly why restoring the existing contract usually serves a client better than being rewritten, since a new policy is newly underwritten at current age and health and generally restarts contestability and suicide provisions. Rewriting a client's own lapsed policy to produce a fresh first-year commission where reinstatement would have served them is the specific abuse this unit exists to prevent.

included: grace, automatic premium loan and non-forfeiture provisions as contract classes
the reinstatement process and its evidence and time limits
diagnosing why payment stopped before proposing a fix
the reinstate-versus-rewrite comparison stated on client grounds
excluded: the full suitability analysis behind any genuinely new coverage
the replacement transaction process and its disclosure forms
carrier underwriting decisions on a reinstatement application

pros.claim: A settled procedure produces the right answer under time pressure, when improvisation reliably favours whichever option pays the agent
pros.example: a documented rule that reinstatement is examined and priced before any new application is discussed on a lapsed policy

pros.claim: Diagnosing the cause first prevents solving the wrong problem
pros.example: discovering the draft failed because of a closed account rather than hardship, which turns a save conversation into a two-minute form

cons.claim: Reinstatement is not always available or best, and a rigid preference for it can waste a client's time or leave them uninsured while an application is underwritten
cons.example: a client whose health has deteriorated facing evidence-of-insurability requirements that a reinstatement cannot clear

cons.claim: The work is time-critical and emotionally uncomfortable, so it is the first thing a busy practice quietly stops doing
cons.example: grace-period calls deferred through a heavy issue week and made after the window closed

failure_modes: proposing a replacement policy before checking whether the existing contract can simply be cured or reinstated
reciting reinstatement terms from another carrier's contract instead of reading this one
letting the agent's own debit-balance exposure decide which option is presented to the client
acceptance_tests: for each policy that entered grace, the file records the cause of non-payment, the option set presented, the client's decision and the date
no lapsed policy was rewritten without a recorded comparison against reinstatement stating why the rewrite served the client better
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes its reinstatement requirements, window or evidence standard
the save rate on grace-period cases drops materially
a rewrite is found in the file without the comparison note

base.update_signal: a carrier changes reinstatement terms, or the file shows rewrites without a documented reinstatement comparison

nodes.definition: Operate the desk that processes what clients actually ask for after the sale, and hold the line where administration becomes advice. The routine traffic: address, name and contact changes; beneficiary changes; ownership changes and assignments; payment mode and method changes; duplicate contract requests; premium, status and value inquiries; loan, partial withdrawal and surrender inquiries on contracts with cash value; rider changes; and reinstatement paperwork. For each request type the practice needs the carrier's current form, who must sign it and in what capacity, what proof or witnessing is required, a realistic turnaround, and a confirmation step that sends the carrier's own acknowledgement back to the client rather than the agent's assurance that it was handled. The judgment that makes this a work unit rather than a clerical task is the boundary test: a purely administrative change is executed and confirmed, but any request that changes coverage, cost or benefits - reducing face amount, dropping a rider, taking a policy loan, electing a non-forfeiture option, surrendering for cash - stops being administration and becomes a recommendation, which means the consequences are explained first and the request is routed through the needs and suitability process before it is acted on. Speed is a service value here, but a fast execution of a change the client did not understand is a failure, not a service.

included: the in-force request catalogue with forms, signatures, proofs and turnarounds
confirmation to the client using the carrier's own acknowledgement
the administrative-versus-recommendation boundary test and the routing that follows it
excluded: the suitability analysis behind any coverage change
carrier processing and underwriting decisions
drafting or interpreting trusts, assignments or settlement instructions

pros.claim: A catalogued desk turns unpredictable client requests into repeatable work with a known turnaround, which is most of what clients mean by good service
pros.example: a beneficiary change completed on the correct current form the first time instead of being rejected and repeated weeks later

pros.claim: The boundary test prevents the most common quiet harm in servicing: an irreversible value decision executed as if it were paperwork
pros.example: a surrender request paused so the client understands what is given up and what the alternatives are before anything is signed

cons.claim: Applying the boundary test slows requests the client experiences as simple, and some clients read the pause as obstruction
cons.example: a client wanting a quick loan against cash value who is frustrated by an explanation of how the loan and its interest affect the contract

cons.claim: Service volume scales with the book and quietly consumes the capacity reserved for reviews and new business
cons.example: a growing book where request handling absorbs the time the cadence plan had allocated to annual reviews

failure_modes: using an outdated carrier form, which turns a two-week change into a two-month one
confirming completion from the agent's own record rather than from the carrier's acknowledgement
executing a coverage-, cost- or benefit-changing request as routine administration because the client asked for it plainly
acceptance_tests: each request type in the catalogue names the current carrier form, the required signatures and proofs, the expected turnaround and the confirmation artifact
every request that changed coverage, cost or benefits in the period shows a recorded consequence explanation and a suitability routing before execution
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes a form, a signature requirement or its processing turnaround
a client complaint or a rejected submission reveals a gap in the catalogue
request volume grows past the desk's response-window capacity

base.update_signal: a carrier changes forms or turnarounds, or a complaint reveals a request type handled outside the boundary test

nodes.definition: Keep the fields that decide where the money actually goes verified and current across the entire book, on a cycle rather than on hope. The work: confirm primary and contingent beneficiaries as recorded by the carrier rather than as remembered by anyone; check that each designation is specific enough to be administered without dispute; verify the policy owner and any assignment or collateral interest; confirm the insured's and owner's contact records; and re-verify all of it at every scheduled review and after any life event the client discloses. The mechanism that makes this the highest-stakes clerical work in the practice is blunt: the carrier pays according to the designation on file at the date of death, so a designation never updated after a divorce, a remarriage, a death or the birth of a child sends the entire benefit to someone the policy was not bought for, and nothing done afterwards repairs it. The agent's role is bounded and specific - prompt the review, supply the correct carrier form, confirm from the carrier's acknowledgement that the change was actually recorded, and file it - while staying strictly out of drafting or interpreting trusts, wills, marital agreements or settlement instructions, which belong to the client's own attorney and where an agent's helpfulness becomes practising law.

included: verifying designations, owner and assignments against the carrier's own record
the re-verification cycle and life-event triggers
confirming recorded changes from the carrier acknowledgement
excluded: drafting or interpreting trusts, wills, marital agreements or settlement instructions
estate, tax or legal advice about who should be named
claim adjudication and settlement administration

pros.claim: Verification against the carrier's record catches the gap between what the client believes and what the carrier will act on
pros.example: a client certain their new spouse is named discovering at a review that the change form was never processed and the prior designation still stands

pros.claim: A fixed cycle turns an uncomfortable question into a normal, expected part of servicing
pros.example: asking about designations at every review as routine, so the divorced client is not singled out for a difficult conversation

cons.claim: Designation conversations open family circumstances the agent is neither qualified nor entitled to advise on, and the pull to help is strong
cons.example: a client asking whether to name a trust or a minor child, which is an attorney's question that an agent's opinion can only damage

cons.claim: The work is invisible until a claim, so it is chronically under-resourced against activities with visible output
cons.example: a review season where designation verification is dropped to fit more appointments in

failure_modes: accepting the client's recollection of who is named instead of checking the carrier record
submitting a change and never confirming from the carrier that it was recorded
answering the question of who should be named, rather than routing it to the client's attorney
acceptance_tests: every policy carries a dated verification of beneficiary, contingent beneficiary, owner and any assignment, taken from the carrier's record
every submitted designation change has a matching carrier acknowledgement in the file, and no file contains agent-authored trust or estate wording
revisit_triggers: a client discloses a marriage, divorce, birth, adoption or death in the family
a claim or a review reveals a designation that was never recorded as instructed
a carrier changes its designation forms or its administrability requirements

base.update_signal: a claim or review reveals an unrecorded designation change, or a carrier changes its designation requirements

nodes.definition: Define exactly what happens when an insured dies, because this is the single event the entire book exists for and the one on which the practice's reputation is permanently settled. The protocol: respond immediately and personally, in whatever channel the family has used, and before anything administrative say the human thing; identify the correct claimant and the carrier's claim unit; explain the document classes the carrier will require - its own claim forms and a certified death certificate are the usual core, with additional requirements where death occurs within the contestable period or in circumstances the contract addresses; help the family assemble and submit while leaving to them whatever must genuinely be theirs to sign and attest; set honest expectations about timing and about what a routine contestable-period review is, so an ordinary verification is not experienced as an accusation; explain the settlement options the contract offers as classes, without steering toward any of them; and follow through with the carrier until the claim is paid, keeping the family informed even when there is nothing new. The boundaries are absolute: no advice on how to invest, hold or use the proceeds, no tax or legal opinions, no prediction of the amount or the date, and no attempt at any point to turn a grieving family into a sales conversation - a fact that, ironically, is also why this unit generates more durable business than any prospecting activity in the practice.

included: the response sequence and claimant identification
document classes the carrier will require and realistic expectation-setting
explaining contestable-period review and settlement option classes neutrally
following the claim through to payment
excluded: claim adjudication, contest or rescission decisions
tax, legal or investment advice on proceeds and any recommendation about what to do with the money
selling anything to the family during the claim

pros.claim: Competent, present claim service is the only proof the product works, and it is the strongest durable source of new relationships a practice ever gets
pros.example: a family who watched the agent handle a claim calmly introducing them to relatives years later without being asked

pros.claim: Explaining a contestable-period review in advance prevents an ordinary verification from being experienced as bad faith
pros.example: a beneficiary told at the outset why the carrier is requesting records, who then waits without panic

cons.claim: Claim work arrives without warning, cannot be scheduled, and displaces whatever the calendar held
cons.example: a claim landing in review season and consuming days that had been booked for appointments

cons.claim: The agent's presence at an emotional moment creates an opportunity to sell that is profitable, easy to rationalize and corrosive
cons.example: raising the beneficiary's own coverage gap while the claim is still open, framed as care

failure_modes: going quiet because there is no news, which the family experiences as abandonment
answering tax or investment questions about the proceeds instead of routing them to the family's own professionals
promising a payment date or amount the carrier has not confirmed
acceptance_tests: every claim in the period shows a same-cycle first response, the documents requested, a contact log through to payment, and no product discussion in the record before the claim closed
the file shows settlement options explained as classes with no recommendation, and any tax or legal question referred out
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes its claim requirements, forms or unit contacts
a family reports the process was unclear or slow
a claim arises inside the contestable period or in circumstances the contract treats specially

base.update_signal: a carrier changes claim requirements, or a family reports the claim experience fell short

nodes.definition: Decide who gets contacted how often, and prove the promise is physically deliverable before it is made. Segment the book on service need rather than on premium alone: contract complexity (a permanent contract with a ledger that can drift needs periodic attention that a level term policy simply does not), life stage and volatility, vulnerability, how concentrated the household's whole protection is in one contract, whether a contractual deadline is approaching, and how long it has been since anyone spoke to them. Assign each segment a cadence class - a scheduled full review, a lighter periodic touch, or event-driven contact only - and then do the arithmetic honestly: cadence multiplied by segment size gives annual contact volume, contact volume multiplied by realistic minutes per contact including preparation and file notes gives required hours, and that total has to fit inside the hours genuinely available after new business, service requests and administration, with slack held back for claims and grace-period work that never wait for a free calendar. Where it does not fit, there are four honest responses - change the cadence, systematize or delegate the light touches, add capacity, or stop growing - and one dishonest one, which is to promise a cadence that will silently fail, always on the smallest policyholders first, who are usually the households least able to replace what they lose.

included: need-based segmentation criteria
cadence classes per segment
contact-volume-to-hours arithmetic with slack for claims and saves
the honest responses when the promise exceeds capacity
excluded: the content of a review itself
prospect contact and lead-generation cadence
hiring, delegation contracts and staffing arrangements as an employment matter

pros.claim: Capacity arithmetic makes an over-promised service model visible before clients discover it
pros.example: finding that the promised annual review for every household needs more hours than the year contains, and adjusting the promise rather than quietly failing it

pros.claim: Need-based segmentation directs attention where policies actually fail rather than where premium is largest
pros.example: giving an underfunded permanent contract more attention than a larger, stable level term case that needs almost nothing

cons.claim: Any segmentation risks becoming a service tier that abandons small policyholders, who are often the most vulnerable buyers in the book
cons.example: a final-expense segment placed on event-driven contact only and then never contacted, because no event ever generates a signal

cons.claim: Capacity limits create pressure to keep writing new business anyway, since the cost of over-selling appears years later while the cost of not selling appears this month
cons.example: a practice that keeps adding cases at a rate its own arithmetic says it cannot service

failure_modes: segmenting by premium size and calling it service need
computing capacity without slack, so the first claim or grace-period cluster destroys the schedule
promising a cadence in the sales process that the practice has never tested against its own hours
acceptance_tests: every in-force household sits in exactly one segment with a stated cadence and a named reason for that segment
the computed required hours for the promised cadence fit available hours with explicit slack reserved for claims and grace-period work
revisit_triggers: the book grows, or an orphan block is absorbed
the practice loses or adds service capacity
a segment shows persistency or complaint results diverging from the rest of the book

base.update_signal: book size, capacity or a segment's persistency and complaint results change

nodes.definition: Run the periodic review as a service event with a fixed agenda and a documented output, not as an appointment whose purpose depends on what turns up. The agenda: confirm from the carrier's own record that the policy is in force and premium is current; verify owner, insured, beneficiary and contingent beneficiary; confirm contact details and stated preferences; for contracts with cash value, obtain and read a current in-force ledger against what the policy was expected to do; check whether any contractual option window or level-period end is approaching; ask directly what has changed in the household since the last review, using the life-event map as a checklist rather than a script; restate in plain language what the coverage does today and what it does not; and record what the client decided. The output is a file note stating what was reviewed, what was found, what if anything was recommended, what was disclosed, and what the client chose - because a review that leaves no record cannot later be shown to have happened, and the times that matter are exactly the times nobody can remember. The defining discipline is that a review is complete and successful when nothing needs to change and nothing is sold; an agent who cannot conduct that review has a sales appointment with a review's name on it.

included: the fixed review agenda
verification from carrier records rather than recollection
the documented file-note output
the rule that a review with no change is a successful review
excluded: the suitability analysis and product selection behind any new recommendation
the replacement process where existing coverage would be displaced
prospecting appointments dressed as reviews

pros.claim: A fixed agenda makes the review reproducible and defensible instead of dependent on the agent's mood or the client's talkativeness
pros.example: designation verification and deadline checks happening on every review, including the ones where the client only wanted to chat

pros.claim: The documented file note is the practice's only durable evidence of what was said years later
pros.example: a note showing a client was told their level period ends and declined to convert, written the day it happened

cons.claim: Reviews are the largest recurring time cost in a service model and produce no visible revenue in the period they consume
cons.example: a review season that displaces new-business activity and shows up immediately in submitted cases and not at all in this year's income

cons.claim: The review is the most natural moment to sell, which makes it the point where servicing and selling are hardest to keep separate
cons.example: an agent who finds nothing wrong reaching for a product discussion because the appointment otherwise feels unproductive

failure_modes: conducting the review from memory and the client's account instead of from carrier records and a current ledger
leaving no file note, so the review cannot be evidenced
treating a review with no change as a wasted appointment
acceptance_tests: every completed review has a dated file note covering in-force status, designations, contact preferences, deadlines checked, changes discussed, disclosures made and the client's decision
reviews where nothing changed are recorded as completed reviews with the same documentation as any other
revisit_triggers: the agenda misses something a later problem shows it should have caught
review completion rates fall behind the cadence the segment promises
a carrier changes the in-force reporting the review depends on

base.update_signal: a missed issue reveals an agenda gap, or review completion falls behind the promised cadence

nodes.definition: Read what the carrier actually sent about a contract with cash value and translate it for the client without embellishment. The skills are specific: distinguish the guaranteed columns from the current-assumption columns and state plainly that only the guaranteed basis is contractually promised; determine whether the policy is being funded at, above or below the level its own original projection assumed; recognize the mechanisms that erode an interest-sensitive, universal or indexed contract - cost-of-insurance charges that rise with attained age, crediting below what was projected, a policy loan whose interest capitalizes against the account, partial withdrawals that permanently reduce value, and premium holidays taken years earlier whose effect only appears now; and know when to request a fresh in-force ledger run on both bases so the client sees the range rather than the optimistic edge of it. The output to the client is three plain statements: what happens if nothing changes, what the contract guarantees regardless, and what options exist if the first is unacceptable. What is forbidden is equally specific - presenting a current-assumption projection as an expectation, comparing one contract's current-assumption column against another's guaranteed column, and using an alarming projection as a lever to sell a replacement rather than as information the client uses to decide.

included: separating guaranteed from current-assumption values
diagnosing funding adequacy and the erosion mechanisms
requesting fresh in-force ledgers on both bases
the three plain statements delivered to the client
excluded: point-of-sale illustration presentation and product selection
any projection of dividend scales, crediting rates or market performance
recommending a replacement, which belongs to the suitability process

pros.claim: Reading the ledger early converts a future policy failure into a decision the client can still afford to make
pros.example: an underfunded contract identified while additional premium or a benefit reduction can still stabilize it, rather than at the point it can no longer be saved

pros.claim: Showing both bases makes the agent's honesty structural rather than a matter of character
pros.example: a client who sees the guaranteed and current columns side by side and understands the range without being told what to expect

cons.claim: The honest answer is often unwelcome and can damage trust in the original recommendation, including one the same agent made
cons.example: explaining that a policy sold years ago on optimistic assumptions now needs more premium than the client budgeted

cons.claim: A ledger showing trouble is a powerful selling instrument, which makes it the most conflicted document in the review
cons.example: using a projected lapse date to push a replacement contract rather than presenting the in-contract options first

failure_modes: reading only the current-assumption column because it is the one that reads well
comparing contracts on inconsistent bases so the preferred one looks better than it is
delivering an alarming projection without the guaranteed floor and the in-contract options beside it
acceptance_tests: every ledger discussion in the file shows both the guaranteed and the current-assumption basis and states which one is promised
no comparison in the file uses different bases on the two sides, and every alarming projection is accompanied by the in-contract options
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes crediting, charges or its in-force reporting format
a contract's funding status crosses from adequate to inadequate on the current basis
a client takes a loan or withdrawal that alters the projection

base.update_signal: a carrier changes charges, crediting or ledger formats, or a contract's funding status crosses into inadequacy

nodes.definition: Maintain the calendar of dated contractual rights that expire silently, because nobody else in the client's life is watching them and the client will not discover the loss until it is permanent. The classes to track: a term policy's conversion privilege, which typically ends at a stated age or duration after which converting without new evidence of insurability is no longer available; the end of a level-premium period, after which coverage under many contracts continues only at a premium that steps up steeply and then annually; guaranteed insurability or additional-purchase option windows on contracts that carry them; rider expiries; any election that must be made by a date; and the point at which a contract's own projection shows it needing attention. Every one of these must be read from the actual contract, since terms differ by product, carrier and issue year, and every one must be entered as a dated alert set far enough ahead that the client can genuinely act - which means allowing for a decision conversation, any underwriting the alternative would require, and the carrier's processing time, not merely for a phone call the week before. A missed window is the most irreversible failure in this subdomain: the right does not degrade, it ceases to exist, and no amount of subsequent service recovers it.

included: the dated option and expiry classes
reading each from the actual contract and entering it as an alert
setting lead time that allows for decision, underwriting and processing
excluded: the suitability analysis of whether to exercise an option
carrier underwriting of a conversion or new coverage
post-level-period pricing decisions as a product recommendation

pros.claim: A dated calendar preserves rights that cannot be recreated at any price once they lapse
pros.example: a client in poor health converting a term policy inside the window, which no amount of money would have bought them a month later

pros.claim: Advance warning of a level-period end turns a shocking premium increase into a planned decision
pros.example: a household given a year's notice choosing deliberately between converting, replacing or accepting the step-up, rather than reacting to a bill

cons.claim: Deadline alerts create contact that a client can experience as a sales approach, particularly when the honest answer involves new coverage
cons.example: a conversion-window call read as an upsell attempt by a client who has heard nothing else that year

cons.claim: The calendar is only as good as the contract reading behind it, and reading every contract's option terms is slow, unglamorous work
cons.example: an alert set from a product summary rather than the policy, which turns out to state a different end age

failure_modes: setting alerts from product marketing summaries instead of the issued contract
setting the alert for the deadline itself rather than for the point where action is still possible
tracking deadlines only for the segment that receives full reviews, leaving the rest unwatched
acceptance_tests: every convertible or option-bearing contract in the book has its window recorded from the issued contract with an alert dated to allow decision, underwriting and processing time
no policy left the book through a lapsed option window without a documented prior contact attempt
revisit_triggers: a policy is discovered whose option terms were never read from the contract
a carrier changes conversion or option administration
an alert fires too late for the client to have acted
