base.update_signal: an option window is found unrecorded or an alert fires too late for the client to act

nodes.definition: Keep a working catalogue of the events that change what a household needs or what a policy can do, together with the listening system that actually catches them, since almost none of them will be reported to the agent as news. The events: a birth or adoption; a marriage; a divorce or separation; a death in the family, especially of a spouse or a named beneficiary; a home purchase or a change in mortgage debt; a substantial income change in either direction; a job change that gains or loses group coverage; starting, buying or selling a business; taking on or retiring significant debt; retirement; a serious diagnosis; a beneficiary's own change in circumstances such as disability or divorce; a change in caregiving responsibility; and a move to another state, which can change what applies to the relationship. The listening system is deliberate rather than hopeful: the review agenda asks directly, service contacts capture what is mentioned in passing, and operational signals are read as evidence - returned mail, a name change on a form, a request to reduce premium. Everything heard is written into the record with its date and routed to a response: a records update, a designation review, a coverage conversation subject to the ethics gate, or explicitly nothing. The map's purpose is to notice, never to manufacture urgency; an event is a reason to ask a question, not a script for making a family frightened.

included: the event catalogue
the deliberate listening system across reviews, service contacts and operational signals
dated recording and routing of what is heard
excluded: the needs analysis that would follow a genuine change
any urgency framing or emotional pressure built on an event
monitoring clients through sources they have not consented to

pros.claim: A catalogue turns coverage relevance into something checked rather than remembered, which is the difference between a book that stays useful and one that quietly becomes irrelevant
pros.example: a client whose mortgage was retired and whose children are independent being told their coverage need has fallen, which is a service the agent is not paid for

pros.claim: Reading operational signals as life events catches changes clients never think to report
pros.example: a name change on a beneficiary form prompting a designation review that finds an outdated primary designation

cons.claim: A life-event list is exactly the instrument fear-selling uses, and the same catalogue that enables service enables manipulation
cons.example: using a new baby as an occasion to press a household about what would happen to the child if the parent died tonight

cons.claim: Listening systems collect sensitive household information that then has to be held, protected and justified
cons.example: a file accumulating notes on a client's divorce and health that serve no servicing purpose

failure_modes: hearing an event, doing nothing with it, and having no record that it was ever mentioned
treating every event as a coverage opportunity rather than as a question to ask
collecting and retaining personal detail beyond what servicing the policy requires
acceptance_tests: every event disclosed in the period appears in the record with a date and a routed response, including the responses that were explicitly nothing
no event note in the file is used as the basis of a contact framed around fear, urgency or a family's destitution
revisit_triggers: a client's circumstances change in a way the catalogue does not list
an event was heard and never routed
a jurisdiction or carrier changes what may be recorded and retained about a client

base.update_signal: an event class appears that the catalogue does not cover, or recording and retention rules change

nodes.definition: Install the explicit rule that decides when a service relationship may become a new transaction, and apply it every time without exception, because this is the boundary where a persistency-driven practice is most profitably corrupted. The gate has five conditions. First, a review or service contact may become a recommendation only when a documented change - in the household's circumstances, or in the policy's own performance against what it was expected to do - makes the existing arrangement inadequate. Second, that finding is written down before any product is discussed, so the diagnosis cannot be reverse-engineered from the sale. Third, the client is told plainly what stays the same if they do nothing, and doing nothing is presented as a legitimate outcome rather than as inaction. Fourth, the compensation consequences are disclosed on both sides: what the agent would receive if the change is made, and the fact that keeping the existing policy pays the agent differently - stated as a mechanism, without invented figures. Fifth, if the change would displace existing coverage, the replacement transaction and its disclosure duties in the client's jurisdiction govern in full; that process belongs to the suitability knowledge base and is run there, never summarized here. The gate also names the techniques it forbids: manufactured urgency, fear framing built on a client's death or a family's destitution, capitalizing on a recent bereavement or diagnosis, and pressing any client showing signs of confusion, dependence, isolation or duress - where the required action is to stop, offer to include a trusted contact where permitted and the client agrees, and document the decision to wait.

included: the documented-change precondition and the write-it-first rule
the do-nothing baseline stated to the client
compensation disclosure on both sides as a mechanism
prohibited pressure techniques and the vulnerable-client stop rule
excluded: the suitability analysis and product selection itself
the replacement transaction process and its jurisdiction-specific forms
any specific compensation figure or comparison of amounts

pros.claim: A written gate makes the ethical answer the default one rather than a matter of daily willpower
pros.example: an agent whose own procedure requires the finding in writing before a product is named, which stops the sale that would have been rationalized afterwards

pros.claim: Disclosing the compensation consequence on both sides removes the client's largest unanswered question and usually strengthens the relationship
pros.example: telling a client that keeping the existing policy pays the agent differently than replacing it, before the client wonders

cons.claim: The gate blocks revenue in exactly the moments it is easiest to earn, and its cost is immediate while its benefit is diffuse
cons.example: a review that surfaces a plausible upgrade being closed with no sale because the documented change condition was not met

cons.claim: A procedural gate can be satisfied on paper while the pressure it was built to prevent is applied in the conversation
cons.example: a finding written first and then presented with heavy emotional framing that the file note does not capture

failure_modes: writing the finding after the product discussion so it documents the sale rather than justifying it
presenting doing nothing as negligence rather than as a legitimate choice
continuing a recommendation conversation with a client showing confusion or duress because the client kept agreeing
acceptance_tests: every recommendation arising from a service contact has a dated written finding that precedes any product discussion in the file
every such file records the do-nothing baseline, the compensation disclosure on both sides, and, where coverage would be displaced, the routing into the replacement process
revisit_triggers: a complaint, a regulator inquiry or an internal audit questions a review-generated sale
the ratio of reviews producing sales moves sharply in either direction
a jurisdiction changes its standard of care, disclosure or replacement requirements

base.update_signal: a complaint or audit questions a review-generated sale, or a jurisdiction changes its standard-of-care or replacement rules

nodes.definition: Build referral flow as a system with a trigger, a form of ask, a permission record and a follow-through, rather than as a mood that visits an agent when production is thin. The trigger is an evidenced service outcome: a review completed, a claim paid, a failing draft fixed, a policy reinstated rather than replaced, a designation corrected - something the client experienced, not something the agent asserts. The ask is specific and low-pressure: an offer to be introduced to someone in a situation the practice actually serves, phrased so that refusal costs the client nothing and changes nothing about the service they receive, which is the single condition that separates a referral system from a toll. Service is never conditioned on, delayed by, prioritized by, or improved because of a referral. Every introduction is logged with its source and with the client's explicit permission to use their name; the referred person's own contact preferences govern from the very first contact; and the referring client is told what came of it in general terms without disclosing anything about the referred person's business. The compliance boundary is a class to verify rather than a matter of taste: paying compensation or giving things of value in exchange for referrals is restricted or prohibited in many jurisdictions, rules on inducements and rebating govern what may be offered to a client or a source, and carrier compliance manuals add their own limits - verify current requirements in each state and with each carrier before offering anything of value to anyone.

included: the evidenced-service trigger for an ask
the low-pressure ask form and costless refusal
permission and source logging, and honoring the referred person's preferences
inducement, rebating and referral-compensation limits as classes to verify
excluded: prospecting to strangers, purchased leads and cold contact programs
the needs analysis and sale to the referred prospect
paying or arranging compensation to any referral source without verified authority

pros.claim: Tying the ask to an evidenced service outcome makes referrals a byproduct of the work rather than a separate imposition on the relationship
pros.example: an introduction offered after a claim was paid promptly, when the client has just watched the product do exactly what it promised

pros.claim: A referred relationship generally starts with trust that no acquisition channel manufactures, which shows up later in persistency rather than only in acquisition cost
pros.example: a household introduced by a sibling who already knows how the agent behaved during a claim

cons.claim: Referral asks put a client in a social position they did not choose, and repeated asking converts a service relationship into an obligation
cons.example: a client who begins screening calls because every contact ends with a request for names

cons.claim: Referral flow concentrates the book inside one social or community network, so a single reputational event or a shared economic shock can hit many policies at once
cons.example: a book built almost entirely inside one employer's workforce facing a mass layoff

failure_modes: asking before the service outcome exists, which makes the ask the point of the contact
contacting an introduced person before confirming permission and preferences
offering something of value for referrals without verifying what the jurisdiction and carrier permit
acceptance_tests: every logged introduction records the service outcome that preceded it and the client's explicit permission to use their name
no referral in the period was solicited with anything of value, or any such arrangement is documented against a verified jurisdiction and carrier authority
revisit_triggers: a client signals discomfort with being asked, or referral acceptance drops
inducement, rebating or referral-compensation rules change in a state the practice writes in
the book's source concentration passes the level the practice considers prudent

base.update_signal: referral acceptance shifts, or inducement and referral-compensation rules change in a state the practice writes in

nodes.definition: Develop reciprocal working relationships with the professionals whose clients surface protection needs - accountants, attorneys, mortgage and real-estate professionals, property and casualty agents, benefits and human-resources contacts, and in the final-expense market funeral directors - and run them on service rather than on transactions. What makes one work is unglamorous: give the partner something genuinely useful, starting with a clear statement of what you handle and what you do not; help their clients promptly whether or not a sale results; report back so the partner knows what happened to someone they trusted you with; and stay so firmly inside your own lane that the partner never has to defend the introduction, which in practice means being the person who says in front of a shared client that a question belongs to their accountant or their attorney. The boundaries are firm and must be verified rather than assumed: compensation sharing with unlicensed persons and referral fees are regulated and frequently prohibited, arrangements that tie a professional service to a required insurance purchase can raise anti-tying and inducement concerns, and any client information passing between the two practices carries privacy duties on both sides. The relationship is measured in clients well served over years, not in a count of introductions, and a partner whose introductions consistently produce business the practice should not write is a relationship to end rather than to manage.

included: building and maintaining professional referral relationships on service
the stay-in-your-lane discipline in front of shared clients
compensation-sharing, anti-tying and privacy boundaries as classes to verify
ending relationships that produce unsuitable business
excluded: formal joint ventures, revenue-sharing agreements or paid marketing arrangements without verified authority
advising the partner's clients on the partner's subject matter
prospect lead purchasing and market-focus selection

pros.claim: A professional partner meets clients at the exact moments protection needs become visible, which no advertising channel reproduces
pros.example: an attorney whose client has just formed a business and asked a question the attorney correctly declines to answer

pros.claim: Visible lane discipline is what makes a professional willing to risk their own client relationship on the introduction
pros.example: declining to opine on a tax question in front of a shared client and routing it back to the accountant, which is what earns the next introduction

cons.claim: These relationships take years to produce anything and many never do, which makes them easy to over-invest in on the strength of hope
cons.example: months of coffees with a partner whose client base never actually needed what the practice sells

cons.claim: The compensation question is where these arrangements most often go wrong, and the wrong answer is a licensing and compliance exposure rather than a bad deal
cons.example: an informal per-introduction payment to an unlicensed source that the jurisdiction does not permit

failure_modes: treating the relationship as a lead source and letting it lapse when introductions slow
agreeing to a compensation arrangement without verifying what the jurisdiction and carriers permit
answering the partner's subject-matter questions to look capable, which costs the relationship the moment it is wrong
acceptance_tests: each active partner relationship records what the practice handles and does not, and every client sent in either direction has a documented handoff
any compensation or value exchange with a referral source is documented against a verified jurisdiction and carrier authority, or there is none
revisit_triggers: a partner's introductions produce cases the practice should not write
compensation-sharing or anti-tying rules change in a state the practice operates in
a privacy incident or complaint arises from information passing between the practices

base.update_signal: a partner's introductions change in quality, or compensation-sharing and anti-tying rules change in an operating state

nodes.definition: Decide on evidence rather than appetite whether to take on policies whose writing agent has left, or whose owner wants a different servicing agent, and know exactly what does and does not transfer when you do. The mechanism: an agent-of-record or servicing-agent change is a carrier-administered process that generally requires the policyowner's own written authorization on the carrier's form and the carrier's acceptance, and what it moves is servicing responsibility - it does not automatically move any compensation stream, which may stay with the original writing agent, revert to the agency or the carrier, or transfer only in part, entirely according to the carrier's rules and the agency contract, both of which must be read for the specific block rather than assumed from a previous one. The judgment has three inputs: whether the block's service load fits the practice's measured capacity, what condition its records are in (a block with no service history, stale contact data and unverified designations costs far more to service than its policy count suggests), and whether the relationships can realistically be rebuilt with people who may not know the agent exists. The conduct rules are absolute and are the reason this unit sits in a knowledge base about book building rather than about acquisition: never solicit a change by disparaging the previous agent, never initiate a change the owner did not ask for, never present a servicing change as though it required replacing coverage, and treat an inherited client's first contact as a service call and as nothing else.

included: the owner-authorized carrier-administered change process
separating servicing responsibility from the compensation stream and verifying both per carrier and contract
assessing block service load, record condition and rebuildable relationships against capacity
conduct rules for inherited and transferring clients
excluded: buying a block or negotiating its price and terms
the agency or carrier's internal reassignment policy as a contractual negotiation
replacing any coverage as part of taking over servicing

pros.claim: An unserved block is full of households with real coverage and no one watching their deadlines, so servicing it creates value immediately even where compensation does not follow
pros.example: finding a convertible term policy inside an inherited block whose window closes in months and whose owner has never been contacted about it

pros.claim: Verifying what transfers before accepting the block prevents a service obligation being taken on under a false expectation of income
pros.example: reading the carrier's rules and discovering renewals remain with the writing agent, so the block is accepted for relationship value or declined with open eyes

cons.claim: Orphan blocks arrive with the service cost front-loaded and any benefit deferred, and they consume exactly the capacity the existing book was promised
cons.example: a block whose first year is spent correcting contact data and designations while the practice's own review cadence slips

cons.claim: Taking over servicing puts an agent in front of clients whose policies they did not write and cannot fully explain, which invites the shortcut of replacing rather than understanding
cons.example: an inherited permanent contract the agent finds hard to read being proposed for replacement instead of being learned

failure_modes: assuming compensation follows the servicing change because it did with a different carrier
accepting a block whose service load the practice's own capacity arithmetic cannot carry
opening the inherited relationship with a product conversation rather than a service one
acceptance_tests: for each block or agent-of-record change there is a written record of what the carrier's rules and the agency contract say transfers, dated and sourced
the block's estimated service load was tested against the capacity arithmetic before acceptance, and inherited clients' first contacts are logged as service contacts
revisit_triggers: the carrier or agency changes its agent-of-record or reassignment rules
the absorbed block's service load exceeds the estimate used to accept it
the existing book's cadence performance degrades after an absorption

base.update_signal: a carrier or agency changes agent-of-record rules, or an absorbed block's service load exceeds the accepted estimate

nodes.definition: When a cohort's persistency degrades, run a diagnosis that assigns the loss to a stage before spending another hour on saves, because no amount of retention effort repairs a defect that happened at the point of sale. Test the stages in order and stop at the first that explains the pattern: the sale itself - was the premium beyond what the household could sustain, was the need real and owned by the client rather than by the agent, was the product class right for the objective; onboarding - did the payment mechanism ever successfully collect, was the first-statement expectation set, was the case scored for risk at all; billing - is the failure concentrated on a mode, a method, a draft date or a carrier's retry behaviour; the source - is one lead channel, market segment or referral partner producing structurally weaker business than the rest; the carrier - are its notices, statements, service turnaround or billing practices causing losses the practice cannot see from inside; and capacity - did the segment simply go unserviced because the cadence promise exceeded the hours. Each finding is routed to whoever owns that stage: point-of-sale and product-fit findings belong to the needs and suitability knowledge base, lead-source and market-focus findings to the licensing and market-focus knowledge base, and everything else is fixed here. The fix is recorded with a date so the next cohort becomes the test of whether it worked, which is the only mechanism by which this practice actually learns anything.

included: the ordered stage tests from sale through capacity
routing findings to the practice area that owns them
recording the fix so the next cohort tests it
excluded: performing the point-of-sale suitability correction itself
changing market focus or lead sources, which belongs to the licensing and market-focus knowledge base
carrier selection or termination decisions

pros.claim: Ordered diagnosis stops the practice from answering a sales defect with more service effort, which is the most common and most exhausting error in retention work
pros.example: discovering that a weak cohort was written at premium levels the households never had, which no number of reminder calls would have saved

pros.claim: Dating the fix turns the next cohort into a live experiment rather than another anecdote
pros.example: changing the default draft date after one cohort and reading the following cohort's collection failures as the test of it

cons.claim: Attribution across stages is genuinely uncertain, and a confident diagnosis on thin cohort evidence can send the practice chasing the wrong stage for a year
cons.example: blaming a lead source when the real driver was a carrier's billing change that happened in the same month

cons.claim: The diagnosis frequently indicts the agent's own selling, which makes it the analysis most likely to be quietly skipped
cons.example: a finding that the affordability conversation at the point of sale was optimistic, which is uncomfortable to write down

failure_modes: adding save activity before locating the stage that caused the loss
diagnosing from a single small cohort and treating noise as a finding
routing a point-of-sale finding nowhere, so the same defect is written into the next cohort
acceptance_tests: each degraded cohort has a written diagnosis naming the stage, the evidence for it, the routed owner and the dated fix
the following cohort's result is recorded against the fix as confirmation or refutation
revisit_triggers: a cohort degrades for a cause outside the stage list
a fix is applied and the next cohort shows no change
the measurement definition or product mix changes enough to break cohort comparability

base.update_signal: a cohort degrades for a cause outside the stage list, or an applied fix produces no change in the following cohort

nodes.definition: Maintain the record layer that makes the book simultaneously compliant, defensible and servable by someone other than the person who built it. The content per policy: the contract data and issued designations, the service and review history with dates and outcomes, the disclosures given and when, the complaints received and how they were resolved, the client's stated contact preferences, and the option windows and life events already recorded elsewhere in this knowledge base. The obligations that govern it are classes rather than fixed rules - records must be retained for the periods required by the applicable insurance regulator, by the carrier's own agreement and by any privacy statute, and those periods and requirements differ by jurisdiction and by carrier and must be verified rather than assumed. The custody duties are equally concrete: the health, financial and identity information a book accumulates over years is sensitive, must be stored and transmitted securely, may be disclosed only as permitted, must be collected only to the extent servicing requires, and must be disposed of properly when its retention period ends. Continuity is the other half of the same work: a book whose knowledge lives only in one person's head strands its clients the moment that person is unavailable, so the practice names who services the book in that event, keeps records in a form a successor can actually use, and understands that what gives a book value to a successor is documented service history and current, permissioned client data - not a list of names.

included: per-policy record content including service, review, disclosure and complaint history
retention and privacy duties named as obligation classes to verify
secure custody, minimum collection and proper disposal
successor arrangement and record usability
excluded: jurisdiction-specific retention periods and privacy statute requirements stated as specifics
valuing or selling the book in currency terms
the contractual question of who owns the book, which the affiliation agreement settles

pros.claim: A contemporaneous record is the only thing that can answer a complaint or an audit years later, and it costs almost nothing at the time it is written
pros.example: a dated note showing what was disclosed at a review answering a question raised long after everyone's memory of the meeting has gone

pros.claim: A record layer a successor could use is what stops a book from stranding its clients when the agent is unavailable
pros.example: a named continuity arrangement and usable files meaning a household's claim is handled promptly rather than being discovered by the carrier's own process

cons.claim: Accumulating client information creates a custody liability that grows with the book and never shrinks by itself
cons.example: years of health and financial detail held in a system whose security has not been reviewed since the practice was one person

cons.claim: Documentation discipline is invisible in good times and competes with client-facing work for the same hours
cons.example: file notes deferred through a heavy month and then written from memory, which is exactly when they are least reliable

failure_modes: writing file notes from memory days later rather than at the time
assuming a retention period or a privacy requirement rather than verifying it for the jurisdiction and carrier
keeping records in a personal format nobody else can interpret, which makes continuity impossible
acceptance_tests: every service contact, review, disclosure and complaint in the period appears in the record with a date, and the retention and privacy requirements applied are recorded with their verified source
a named continuity arrangement exists and a person other than the principal can locate a given policy's status, designations and service history from the records alone
revisit_triggers: a jurisdiction or carrier changes retention, privacy or complaint-handling requirements
a security or privacy incident occurs, or a data-handling review finds a gap
the practice changes systems, adds staff, or the continuity arrangement lapses

base.update_signal: retention, privacy or complaint rules change, a data incident occurs, or the continuity arrangement lapses

edges.why_related: what counts as the book and the horizon it is judged on decides what the persistency measurement must count and over what window
the frame's claim that only the continuing stream compounds is empty until the mechanism producing that stream is read per carrier and product
the advance and recovery terms that create exposure sit in the same compensation schedule and contract that define the continuing stream
the driver map is built from cohort evidence about which policies actually terminated early and when
the carrier's recovery of unearned advance is the first and most concrete component of what a lapse costs the practice
the onboarding sequence is designed to close the specific drivers the risk map names, so the map has to exist first
mode, method and draft date are chosen and first exercised during onboarding, which is where the payment mechanism is proven to work
the collection failures the watchlist reacts to are produced by the billing arrangement, so the warning system is built on top of it
the intervention playbook is executed on cases the watchlist surfaces, and its window is only usable if the signal arrived in time
onboarding establishes the contact channels, preferences and expectations the service desk then operates against
designation changes are executed through the service desk's forms, signatures and carrier-acknowledgement discipline
the claim is administered against the designation on file, so the claim protocol inherits whatever the hygiene work did or did not do
segmentation and cadence are set against measured persistency and service need rather than against impressions of who matters
the review is the scheduled event the cadence plan promises, and its volume is what the capacity arithmetic had to accommodate
the in-force ledger is obtained and read as part of the review agenda for contracts with cash value
an approaching option window is one of the segmentation criteria and the alert has to be serviceable inside the cadence plan
the gate exists precisely because the review is the moment a service relationship can turn into a transaction
the same disclosure-first, pressure-free standard that governs a review-generated recommendation governs how introductions may be asked for
retention, privacy and complaint-handling duties bound how requests are documented, what proof is held and how long it is kept
the no-projection-as-promise rule and the do-nothing baseline bound how an in-force ledger may be presented to a client
measured capacity bounds how much new business the practice may take on before the service the referrals were earned by degrades
recorded contact preferences and privacy duties bound how hard and through which channels a watchlist entry may be worked
inducement, compensation-sharing and anti-tying limits bound what may be offered to or accepted from a professional referral partner
the agent's unearned advance on a failing policy points at whichever outcome protects the agent, while the client's interest points at whichever outcome protects their coverage
edges.resolution_rule: the client's coverage and contract interest dominates absolutely: the exposure ledger is bookkeeping and is never an input to the option set presented, and any rewrite of a client's own lapsed policy requires a written comparison showing why reinstatement or cure served them worse

edges.why_related: the review is the richest moment to ask for introductions and also the moment at which an ask most easily converts a service into a transaction the client feels obliged to complete
edges.resolution_rule: the service outcome must be delivered and confirmed before any ask; the ask is optional, refusable at no cost, and never repeated in the same contact, and the review is recorded as complete whether or not an introduction resulted

edges.why_related: absorbing an orphan block grows the book immediately while consuming the very hours the existing book's cadence was promised out of
edges.resolution_rule: capacity dominates growth: a block is absorbed only up to the measured capacity ceiling with slack intact, and otherwise the practice adds capacity first, stages the absorption, or declines it - the existing book's promised cadence is never the funding source

edges.why_related: compensation behaves differently when a policy is kept in force than when a new one is written, so the agent's income and the client's interest can point in opposite directions at exactly the moment of recommendation
edges.resolution_rule: the recommendation must stand on a documented client-benefit finding written before any product is discussed, with the compensation consequence disclosed on both sides as a mechanism; where existing coverage would be displaced the replacement process governs in full and is run in the suitability knowledge base, not summarized

edges.why_related: an honest reading of a struggling contract delivers unwelcome news that can undermine the client's confidence in the original recommendation and in the relationship the review exists to maintain
edges.resolution_rule: disclose the guaranteed basis and the current-assumption basis plainly and in the same breath, never soften a projection into a promise and never sharpen it into an alarm; present the in-contract options before any external alternative and record the client's decision in the review note

edges.why_related: terminations concentrated in the early durations are exactly the events that convert unearned advance into a debit balance
mode, method and draft-date choices move the measured persistency of a cohort without anything changing in the client's intent to stay covered
how a claim is handled is the strongest evidence of service a practice ever produces and is the most durable source of introductions it ever receives
life events generate most of the desk's transaction load, from designation changes after a divorce to mode changes after an income change
the review cycle starts from the dated first review booked at onboarding, so the cadence clock is set at delivery rather than at a later convenient moment
every save and every loss worked through the playbook becomes an input the periodic diagnosis reads for pattern
a diagnosis that lands on the onboarding stage sends a specific correction back into the onboarding sequence, and the next cohort tests it
cohort and segment results retune which segments need more contact and whether the promised cadence was ever deliverable

a claim exposes every record defect at once - an outdated designation, an unrecorded change, stale contact data - and each finding must be fed back into the verification cycle for the rest of the book

both are dated watch systems run over the same book from the same calendar discipline, differing in that one reacts to a signal that has already appeared and the other anticipates a right that will silently expire

conflict_axes.name: production_pace_versus_persistency
conflict_axes.description: Writing more cases raises this month's income and this month's chargeback exposure at once, while serving the cases already written raises the probability they persist but produces nothing visible in the period that pays for it.
poles: maximize the survival of business already placed
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: judge the month on cases still paying at the horizon the book charter sets, and cap new business at the level the capacity arithmetic can service rather than at the level the calendar can sell

conflict_axes.name: agent_exposure_versus_client_route
conflict_axes.description: When a policy is failing, the option that limits the agent's debit balance and the option that best protects the client's coverage are frequently different, and the agent is the only party in the room who knows both.
poles: protect the client's contract and coverage
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the exposure ledger out of the client conversation entirely, present the full in-contract option set including the ones that pay nothing, and require a written comparison before any rewrite of a client's own lapsed policy

conflict_axes.name: promised_cadence_versus_available_hours
conflict_axes.description: A service promise is made per client while capacity is consumed across the whole book, so a cadence that sounds modest at the point of sale becomes undeliverable as the book grows, and it fails silently rather than visibly.
poles: promise the service that wins the relationship
promise only what the hours can carry
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run the contact-volume-to-hours arithmetic before the promise is made, hold slack for claims and grace work, and when it no longer fits change the cadence openly instead of letting it lapse on the smallest policyholders

conflict_axes.name: save_urgency_versus_contact_preference
conflict_axes.description: The intervention that saves a policy needs to reach the client quickly and often, while the client's recorded preferences, privacy duties and dignity limit how, when and how insistently they may be contacted - and the clients hardest to reach are frequently the ones under most financial strain.
poles: contact until the policy is saved
contact only as the client permitted
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: recorded preferences and permitted channels govern; escalate through channels the client agreed to, use a trusted contact only where the client authorized one and the jurisdiction permits, log every attempt, and accept a lost policy over a breached preference

conflict_axes.name: review_as_service_versus_review_as_occasion
conflict_axes.description: The annual review is simultaneously the practice's core service obligation and the single best selling opportunity it has, and the same meeting can be either depending on decisions the client cannot see.
poles: the review is complete when nothing needs to change
the review should produce business to justify its cost
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply the ethics gate every time: no recommendation without a documented change written before any product is named, the do-nothing baseline stated aloud, and reviews that produce nothing recorded as fully successful reviews

conflict_axes.name: persistency_loyalty_versus_honest_replacement
conflict_axes.description: A practice measured on persistency has a standing incentive to keep every policy in force, including contracts that no longer serve the household, which is the mirror image of the churning problem and just as damaging to the client.
poles: keep every policy on the books
let a policy go or be replaced when that is what serves the household
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the client's current objective decides, not the persistency report; where a change is genuinely indicated, run the replacement process in full through the suitability knowledge base and record the persistency loss as a correct outcome

conflict_axes.name: current_assumption_comfort_versus_guaranteed_truth
conflict_axes.description: The current-assumption columns of an in-force ledger are the ones clients want to hear and the ones that make the original recommendation look sound, while only the guaranteed basis is actually promised by the contract.
poles: present the outcome the projection suggests
present only what the contract guarantees as promised
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always show both bases together, state explicitly which one is contractual, never mix bases across a comparison, and pair any alarming projection with the in-contract options before any external alternative is mentioned

conflict_axes.name: growth_by_absorption_versus_service_dilution
conflict_axes.description: Orphan blocks and agent-of-record changes add households and future opportunity at once, but their service cost arrives immediately, is front-loaded on record repair, and is paid out of the capacity the existing book already relies on.
poles: absorb only what can be serviced to standard
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: test each block against the capacity arithmetic and record condition before acceptance, verify separately what servicing and what compensation actually transfer, and stage or decline anything that would consume the slack reserved for claims and saves

conflict_axes.name: referral_growth_versus_relationship_burden
conflict_axes.description: Introductions are the cheapest and highest-trust growth a practice has, and asking for them repeatedly converts a service relationship into a standing obligation that clients discharge by avoiding the agent.
poles: ask only where service has visibly been delivered
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tie every ask to an evidenced service outcome, make refusal costless and never repeat within a contact, log permission before contacting anyone, and treat declining referral flow as a signal about service quality rather than about asking technique

edge_cases.description: A client's bank draft fails twice while they are travelling and unreachable, and the policy enters the grace period with only days left on it
edge_cases.trigger: a returned collection on a client who cannot be reached through any recorded channel before the grace period expires
edge_cases.mitigation: escalate through every channel the client authorized in the onboarding record, contact the authorized secondary contact where one exists and the jurisdiction permits, document each attempt with its timestamp, and prepare the reinstatement route in advance so the client returns to a solved problem rather than a lost contract

edge_cases.description: A client calls asking to reduce the face amount to lower the premium, which would also drop a rider and cannot be reversed at the same terms
edge_cases.trigger: a service request that presents as administrative but changes coverage, cost or benefits
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the boundary test, explain what is permanently given up and what alternatives exist including a mode or method change, route the request through the suitability process before execution, and record the explanation and the client's decision

edge_cases.description: A term policy's level period is ending, the premium is about to step up steeply, and the conversion window has already closed
edge_cases.trigger: a level-period expiry discovered after the contractual conversion right has lapsed
edge_cases.mitigation: state plainly what the contract now permits and what it no longer does without implying a right still exists, work only the options that remain, record how the window was missed, and audit the rest of the book immediately for contracts approaching the same point

edge_cases.description: A universal life contract funded at a minimum level for years arrives at a review projected to fail in the client's seventies, and the client believes it is paid up
edge_cases.trigger: an in-force ledger showing the current-assumption basis diverging sharply from what the client understood the policy to be
edge_cases.mitigation: request fresh ledgers on both bases, explain the erosion mechanism in plain terms, present the in-contract options first - additional premium, benefit reduction, or a non-forfeiture route - and only then consider anything external, running any displacement through the full replacement process

edge_cases.description: A beneficiary designation still names an ex-spouse, and the client mentioned the divorce in conversation two years ago but never signed a change form
edge_cases.trigger: a review or claim revealing a designation that contradicts the client's known circumstances and stated intentions
edge_cases.mitigation: supply the current carrier form immediately, confirm from the carrier's acknowledgement that the change was recorded, refer any question about who should be named or how a decree affects it to the client's attorney, and audit the book for other clients whose disclosed events never produced a form

edge_cases.description: An insured dies inside the contestability period and the carrier opens a routine review, while the family calls the agent in distress believing the claim is being refused
edge_cases.trigger: a death claim arising during the contestable period, or in circumstances the contract addresses specially
edge_cases.mitigation: explain what a contestable-period review is and is not, set an honest expectation about timing without predicting an outcome, keep contact with the family through the silence, help assemble documents the carrier requests, and give no opinion on adjudication

edge_cases.description: A competing agent approaches a long-standing client and proposes both an agent-of-record change and a replacement of the existing coverage, and the client calls to ask what to do
edge_cases.trigger: an external replacement or servicing approach into an existing relationship
edge_cases.mitigation: answer on the contract facts rather than about the other agent, show what the existing coverage does on both ledger bases, state what a replacement would cost the client in new underwriting and restarted contract provisions, disclose your own compensation position on both outcomes, and leave the decision explicitly with the client

edge_cases.description: A client stops responding on every channel and mail is returned undeliverable, while the policy continues to pay by automatic draft
edge_cases.trigger: a paying policy whose owner has become unreachable
edge_cases.mitigation: flag the policy as unserviceable rather than as healthy because it is paying, attempt permitted re-contact routes including any authorized secondary contact, record the attempts, and never let automatic payment substitute for verified designations and current contact data

edge_cases.description: A professional referral partner proposes a fee for each client they send, framed as covering their administrative time
edge_cases.trigger: a referral source requesting compensation or another thing of value
edge_cases.mitigation: treat it as a licensing and inducement question rather than a commercial one, verify what the jurisdiction and each carrier permit before agreeing to anything, decline or restructure where authority cannot be evidenced, and document whatever is agreed

edge_cases.description: An adult child calls asking to change the beneficiary or cancel the policy of an elderly parent who is not on the call, saying the parent asked them to handle it
edge_cases.trigger: a third party requesting a change on behalf of a client who may be vulnerable, isolated or under pressure
edge_cases.mitigation: take no instruction from anyone who is not the policyowner or a properly documented authorized party, speak with the owner directly, slow the transaction rather than accelerate it, involve an authorized trusted contact only where permitted and the owner agrees, and document the decision to wait

edge_cases.description: One issue cohort from a single lead source and market segment lapses at a visibly worse rate than every other cohort in the book
edge_cases.trigger: a cohort persistency result diverging materially from the rest of the book
edge_cases.mitigation: run the ordered stage diagnosis before adding save activity, check whether the sample is large enough to carry the conclusion, route point-of-sale and lead-source findings to the knowledge bases that own them, and date the fix so the next cohort tests it

workflow.action: Write the book charter and fix the judging horizon
workflow.description: State what the in-force book is, over what horizon decisions are judged, and which terms are contract-given rather than chosen
workflow.gate: the charter names what counts as in force, the judging horizon, and the contract-given terms it takes as input

workflow.description: Fix the departure-event taxonomy, group policies into issue cohorts, and adopt the carrier's published window
workflow.artifact: cohort persistency definition and standing report
workflow.gate: each departure event classifies into exactly one named outcome and the stored definition names the window, weighting and exclusions

workflow.action: Map renewal and trail mechanics from the actual contracts
workflow.description: Record per carrier and product how long renewals run, on what basis, under what conditions, and what a policy change does to them
workflow.artifact: per-product compensation-continuation map with sources and dates
workflow.gate: every shelf product has a sourced, dated answer and no forecast uses a figure that was not read from a current schedule

workflow.action: Build the exposure ledger and price a lapse
workflow.description: Track unearned advance by issue vintage against each carrier's recovery rule, reconcile to the carrier statement, and compute the practice's own per-lapse cost band from internal records
workflow.artifact: reconciled exposure ledger and per-lapse cost worksheet
workflow.gate: the ledger reconciles to the latest carrier statement within tolerance and every cost component traces to an internal record or is shown as an explicit unknown

workflow.action: Segment the book and size the cadence against real capacity
workflow.description: Assign every household to a need-based segment and cadence class, then prove the promised contact volume fits available hours with slack
workflow.artifact: segmented service calendar with the capacity arithmetic shown
workflow.gate: every household sits in exactly one segment with a stated reason, and required hours fit available hours with slack reserved for claims and grace work

workflow.action: Score issued cases for early-duration risk
workflow.description: Score each delivered case against the named drivers at delivery and assign the action each driver implies
workflow.gate: every case issued in the period carries a driver note and each named driver maps to an owned onboarding or watchlist action

workflow.description: Confirm the payment mechanism has actually collected, set first-statement expectations, verify issued designations, capture channels and preferences, and book the first review
workflow.artifact: onboarding confirmation letter and dated file note
workflow.gate: the file shows a confirmed first collection, verified owner and beneficiary from the issued contract, recorded preferences, and a dated first review

workflow.action: Stand up the lapse-warning watchlist and the save playbook
workflow.description: Map every carrier and client signal to a trigger, an owner and a response window, add compensating checks where a carrier does not notify, and settle the grace and reinstatement decision procedure in advance
workflow.artifact: watchlist with per-carrier notification map and a written save playbook
workflow.gate: every carrier's notification behaviour is recorded with a compensating check where needed, and the playbook states the reinstate-versus-rewrite comparison on client grounds

workflow.action: Open the in-force service desk with the boundary test
workflow.description: Catalogue each request type with its current form, signatures, proofs, turnaround and confirmation artifact, and define which requests become recommendations
workflow.artifact: service request catalogue and request log
workflow.gate: each request type names its form, proofs and confirmation artifact, and every coverage-, cost- or benefit-changing request in the period shows a consequence explanation and suitability routing

workflow.action: Build the contractual deadline and life-event watch calendar
workflow.description: Read every option window from the issued contracts and enter alerts with lead time for decision, underwriting and processing, alongside the life-event listening routine
workflow.artifact: dated option-window calendar covering the whole book
workflow.gate: every option-bearing contract has its window recorded from the issued contract with an alert dated to leave real time to act

workflow.action: Run the review cycle under the ethics gate
workflow.description: Execute the fixed review agenda, read in-force ledgers on both bases, and apply the gate before any review-generated recommendation
workflow.artifact: review file notes with findings, disclosures and client decisions
workflow.gate: every review has a dated note covering status, designations, preferences, deadlines and decisions, and every recommendation has a written finding preceding any product discussion

workflow.action: Open the referral channel and close the diagnostic loop
workflow.description: Ask for introductions only against evidenced service outcomes, and diagnose every degraded cohort by ordered stage, routing findings to the practice area that owns them
workflow.artifact: referral log with permissions plus a dated cohort diagnosis and fix record
workflow.gate: each introduction records the service outcome and permission behind it, and each degraded cohort has a stage diagnosis, a routed owner, a dated fix and a following-cohort result

dominance_rules.rule: The client's coverage interest dominates the agent's compensation position in every in-force decision
dominance_rules.rationale: the agent is the only party who can see both, which is exactly why the rule has to be absolute rather than situational
dominance_rules.trigger: any save, replacement, surrender, loan or servicing decision where the agent's income differs across the options
dominance_rules.action: present the full option set including options that pay the agent nothing, keep the exposure ledger out of the conversation, and document the client-benefit reason for whatever is chosen

dominance_rules.rule: The contract and the carrier's own record dominate memory, marketing summaries and peer accounts
dominance_rules.rationale: everything material in this subdomain - grace terms, reinstatement windows, conversion rights, designations, compensation continuation - varies by contract, carrier and issue year
dominance_rules.trigger: any statement about what a policy does, who is named on it, or what compensation continues
dominance_rules.action: read it from the issued contract, the carrier's record or the current compensation schedule, and record the source and date

dominance_rules.rule: Guaranteed-basis disclosure dominates current-assumption optimism whenever policy values are discussed
dominance_rules.rationale: only the guaranteed basis is contractually promised, and a projection presented as an expectation is the industry's most damaging recurring failure
dominance_rules.trigger: any in-force ledger, annual statement or value comparison presented to a client
dominance_rules.action: show both bases together, state which is promised, never mix bases across a comparison, and pair any alarming projection with the in-contract options

dominance_rules.rule: A contractual deadline dominates the routine service calendar
dominance_rules.rationale: an option window that closes is gone permanently, while a review deferred by a month is recoverable
dominance_rules.trigger: an approaching conversion window, level-period end, option election date or grace expiry
dominance_rules.action: preempt the scheduled cadence, contact the client with enough lead time for a decision plus any underwriting and processing, and record the contact whatever the outcome

dominance_rules.rule: Claim service dominates every other item on the calendar
dominance_rules.rationale: the claim is the only moment at which the product either works or does not, and it cannot be rescheduled
dominance_rules.trigger: notification of a death or a claim inquiry from any source
dominance_rules.action: respond in the same cycle, reassign whatever the calendar held, and stay with the family through to payment

dominance_rules.rule: Vulnerable-client protection dominates transaction speed and client insistence alike
dominance_rules.rationale: a transaction completed by someone who could not weigh it is a harm regardless of how willingly it was signed
dominance_rules.trigger: signs of confusion, dependence, isolation, grief or third-party pressure around any coverage or beneficiary decision
dominance_rules.action: slow the transaction, deal only with the policyowner or a properly documented authorized party, offer to include a trusted contact where permitted and the owner agrees, and document the decision to wait

dominance_rules.rule: Recorded contact preferences and privacy duties dominate outreach intensity, including on save attempts
dominance_rules.rationale: a policy saved by breaching a client's stated preferences costs more relationship and compliance exposure than it recovers
dominance_rules.trigger: any watchlist, review, referral or marketing contact
dominance_rules.action: use only permitted channels and frequencies, log every attempt, and accept a lost policy rather than a breached preference

dominance_rules.rule: The suitability and replacement process dominates any recommendation generated by a service contact
dominance_rules.rationale: a recommendation arising from a review carries the same duties as one arising from a sale, and the review setting makes it easier to skip them
dominance_rules.trigger: a review or service contact that surfaces a possible new sale or a displacement of existing coverage
dominance_rules.action: write the finding first, disclose the compensation consequence on both sides, and route the case into the full needs, suitability and replacement process before any application

dominance_rules.rule: Measured capacity dominates growth of any kind
dominance_rules.rationale: service that fails silently damages the book more than the growth adds, and it fails first on the households least able to absorb it
dominance_rules.trigger: an orphan block offer, a referral surge, or a production target that would exceed the serviceable ceiling
dominance_rules.action: test the addition against the capacity arithmetic with slack intact, and stage, decline or add capacity rather than dilute the promised cadence

dominance_rules.rule: Reinstating or curing an existing contract dominates rewriting it, absent a documented client-benefit reason
dominance_rules.rationale: a rewrite restarts underwriting at current age and health and generally restarts contract provisions the client has already lived through
dominance_rules.trigger: any lapsed or lapsing policy where a new application is being considered
dominance_rules.action: price and present the cure and reinstatement routes first, and record a written comparison if a rewrite is nonetheless recommended

dominance_rules.rule: Factual consequence stated once dominates emotional pressure repeated
dominance_rules.rationale: fear-selling produces business that lapses and relationships that end, and it is the technique this subdomain is most exposed to because the agent knows the household's fears
dominance_rules.trigger: any conversation about death, dependants, debt or a family's financial survival
dominance_rules.action: state the consequence plainly one time, present the options, leave the decision with the client, and never revisit the same fear as a closing device

anti_rework_rules.rule: Define the departure-event taxonomy and the persistency window before building any retention program
anti_rework_rules.prevents: months of retention effort aimed at a number that mixes non-taken cases, expiries and death claims and therefore cannot locate a cause

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read each carrier's renewal, vesting, advance and recovery terms before forecasting income or budgeting on advances
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a practice built on an assumed compensation stream, and a debit balance whose recovery rule is discovered only when it is enforced

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the payment mechanism has actually collected once before closing the onboarding file
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the most preventable class of early termination, and the reacquisition cost of rewriting a case that never failed for a real reason

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture contact channels, preferences and any authorized secondary contact at delivery, not when a policy is already in grace
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unreachable client during the one window in which a failing policy can still be saved

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify owner and beneficiary against the issued contract at onboarding rather than trusting the application
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a designation defect that stays invisible for years and is discovered at the claim, when it can no longer be corrected

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compute service capacity before promising a cadence or accepting an orphan block
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a service promise that fails silently on the smallest policyholders and an absorption that consumes the slack reserved for claims

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record every contractual option window from the issued contract at the time the policy is placed
anti_rework_rules.prevents: conversion privileges and option windows discovered after they closed, which no later service recovers

anti_rework_rules.rule: Diagnose the stage a lapse cohort failed at before adding save activity
anti_rework_rules.prevents: answering a point-of-sale or product-fit defect with retention effort, which exhausts the practice and repeats the defect in the next cohort

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the service and review file note at the time of the contact
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing years later what was disclosed and decided, which cannot be done and is exactly what a complaint or audit asks for

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify what servicing and what compensation actually transfer before working an orphan block or an agent-of-record change
anti_rework_rules.prevents: taking on a front-loaded service obligation under a false expectation of income, and unwinding client relationships built on that expectation

iteration_protocol.trigger: a cohort's persistency degrades relative to the rest of the book
iteration_protocol.action: run the ordered stage diagnosis before adding save activity, route the finding to the practice area that owns it, and date the fix so the next cohort tests it

iteration_protocol.trigger: unearned advance or a debit balance exceeds the practice's stated tolerance
iteration_protocol.action: reconcile the ledger to the carrier statements, re-examine the billing arrangements behind the affected vintage, and re-price the per-lapse cost band

iteration_protocol.trigger: a carrier changes its compensation schedule, billing behaviour, notice practice or service forms
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the affected terms from the source, update the per-product map, the watchlist notification map and the request catalogue, and date the update

iteration_protocol.trigger: the book grows, an orphan block is absorbed, or service capacity changes
iteration_protocol.action: recompute the capacity arithmetic, re-segment the book, and adjust the promised cadence openly rather than letting it fail

iteration_protocol.trigger: a client discloses a life event or a review finds the household's circumstances have changed
iteration_protocol.action: record it with a date, update designations and records, and route any coverage question through the ethics gate before it becomes a recommendation

iteration_protocol.trigger: a claim is handled, whether it went well or badly
iteration_protocol.action: debrief the claim against the protocol, feed every record defect it exposed back into the verification cycle for the rest of the book, and note any introduction the family offered without being asked

iteration_protocol.trigger: an in-force ledger shows a contract off-track on the current-assumption basis
iteration_protocol.action: request fresh ledgers on both bases, present the in-contract options first, and record the client's decision in the review note

iteration_protocol.trigger: a complaint, a missed option window, or a records or privacy incident occurs
iteration_protocol.action: reconstruct what the records show, verify the applicable retention and privacy obligations for the jurisdiction and carrier, correct the process that allowed it, and audit the book for the same exposure elsewhere

priority_rationale: The frame and measurement nodes come first because every retention decision downstream is judged against what the book is, over what horizon, and by a persistency number that has to be reproducible before it can be managed; the compensation and exposure nodes follow because they are the mechanism by which persistency becomes money and the reason an agent's own interest can diverge from the client's; the retention operations sit next because onboarding, billing, warning and grace work are where policies are actually kept or lost and where the cheapest interventions live; the cadence, review, ledger and deadline nodes then organize the ongoing obligation and are the ones whose failures are irreversible; the ethics gate sits above everything that turns servicing into selling; and the growth and governance nodes come last because referrals, absorbed blocks and continuity all compound only on top of service that already demonstrably works.
